fundamental.thesis: TCS is India's largest IT services company (₹8L cr market cap, near-debt-free with filing-reported D/E 0.099 and ROE 51%), serving global clients across BFSI (39.1% of revenue), Manufacturing, and Consumer verticals with dominant scale and 12-year consecutive top-ranked customer satisfaction. At 16.3× trailing P/E — a 33.7% discount to the IT sector peer median of 24.7× and cheapest in sector on forward P/E at 13.4× — TCS screens unambiguously cheap versus both sector peers and the benchmark range of 22–30×, with a pristine balance sheet (CFO/PAT 0.94×, FCF ₹23,768 cr in H1) providing a durable floor; the P/E yardstick is used here as primary per the asset-light IT services model, and EV/EBITDA at 11.1× (P17 in sector vs median 14.7×) corroborates the cheap read. The central risk is AI-led productivity deflation continuing to compress legacy T&M revenues in constant-currency terms: if INR stabilises from current weakness, CC growth likely reverts to near-zero or negative, the INR acceleration collapses, and the re-rating catalyst disappears, leaving TCS cheap but with no near-term earnings growth to close the discount.

fundamental.thesis: M&M is India's dominant auto-farm conglomerate holding #1 positions across SUVs (25.3% share, +260 bps YoY), LCVs (52.3%), tractors (43.6%), and e-3-wheelers (40%), with further exposure to financial services (MMFSL), IT (TechM), real estate, and hospitality — a diversified conglomerate structure that blends cyclical and defensive earnings. Q1 FY27 delivered consolidated revenue of ₹58,188 cr (+27.8% YoY) and PAT of ₹5,455 cr (+33.6% YoY), sustaining a remarkably consistent multi-quarter growth corridor of +25–28% revenue and +33–37% PAT, with PAT margins expanding from 8.6% (FY26) to 9.4% (Q1 FY27); guidance raised twice and then maintained once signals management confidence is intact. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick (appropriate for a capital-intensive OEM with a large NBFC subsidiary), M&M trades at 10.7× vs the sector peer median of 18.3×, ranking at P17 in its peer set — unambiguously cheap; trailing P/E of 19.5× is also at the lower quartile of the 18–28× Auto OEM sector range (P20 vs peers), though the stock sits at only 15.5% of its 52-week range, signalling downward momentum that could persist before fundamentals reassert. The single biggest risk is the sequential compression in the automotive PBIT margin from 9.3% in Q4FY26 to 7.7% in Q1 FY27, combined with rising crude costs (+headwind on vehicle input costs), EV mix dipping from 9.6% to 6.4% quarter-on-quarter, and a sustained RISK_OFF FII outflow environment that keeps the Auto sector on underweight — this cocktail can extend the share-price slide meaningfully before cheap valuations matter to the market.

fundamental.thesis: Sun Pharma is India's largest pharma company by revenue. Its earnings come from leadership in Indian branded formulations, where market share rose 0.3pp to 8.6% and formulations sales grew 16.6% in H1, and from a growing global innovative-medicines (specialty) business that is now about 21.5% of sales. H1FY27 revenue grew 11.0% YoY to ₹31,499 cr, and Q2 (₹16,315 cr, worked out as H1 minus Q1) grew 11.8%, a little faster than Q1's 10.1%. The bigger trend is slowing: growth was +15.1% in 9MFY26, and EBITDA margin has slipped from 31.9% to about 29%. Implied Q2 reported PAT of about ₹1,988 cr gives only a 12.2% margin after large Organon-acquisition and US pricing-settlement charges, and US formulations fell 8.2% in Q2 as Lenalidomide sales eroded. On the yardstick that suits a branded/specialty pharma, valuation is fair. Trailing P/E is 37.4x, inside the 28–40x sector band and at P54 among peers. Forward P/E of 27.7x (P62) and EV/EBITDA of 24.2x (13% above the peer median) leave no room for a re-rating. The biggest risk is integrating the USD 14bn Organon deal. It is several times Sun's ~₹17.7k cr net cash, so the clean balance sheet will likely take on debt, and more deal costs are flagged for coming quarters. Meanwhile sell-side EPS estimates have been cut 2.9–3.4% over 90 days.

fundamental.thesis: NTPC is India's largest power generator. Most of its earnings come from a regulated return (about 15.5% ROE) on the plants it has commissioned, with a fast-growing solar and renewables arm on top. H1 FY27 headline revenue was ₹100,262 cr, up 19.9% from ₹83,660 cr a year ago, but the company's core capacity-plus-energy billing grew a more modest 9.65%. Within that, capacity charges rose 6.7% to ₹35,909 cr, energy charges rose 11.6% to ₹55,845 cr and solar revenue rose 64.9% to ₹2,456 cr. Revenue growth has turned up from about -1.5% to -3% in FY26 to +7.0% in Q1 FY27 (PAT ₹6,896 cr, +12.9%, 13.6% margin), though H1 PAT was not extracted. For a capital-intensive utility I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, backed by P/B with ROE. On that basis it looks cheap against peers: EV/EBITDA is 8.4x against a peer median of 11.6x (cheapest in the peer group) and trailing P/E is 11.9x against 14.7x. P/B is 1.7x with ROE of 13.7%. It is only fair against the static 10–18x utilities P/E band. The forward P/E (12.8x) is above the trailing P/E, and this year's EPS estimates were trimmed 0.9% in the last 30 days, so near-term earnings look roughly flat. The main risk is earnings quality: CERC 2024 tariff orders are still pending, so bills are provisional and later adjusted (₹2,825 cr energy adjustment in H1), and large regulatory-deferral and deferred-tax swings make reported PAT hard to compare across periods.

fundamental.thesis: HCL Technologies is India's #3 IT services company with a differentiated HCLSoftware products arm, competing globally in cloud, AI, and enterprise services — a revenue-mix edge over pure-play peers TCS and Infosys that should sustain margin resilience through the sector's AI-reset cycle. Q1FY27 (latest extracted period) revenue accelerated to +13.9% YoY at ₹34,579 cr after a soft Q4FY26 (+3.9%), with PAT growing +20.3% YoY to ₹4,624 cr and PAT margin expanding to 13.4%; deal TCV of ₹12,275 cr in Q1FY27 (vs ₹3,595 cr in Q3FY26) confirms pipeline build, and the launch of HCLTech AI Platforms Limited in July 2026 reflects execution intent beyond commentary — though per the sector card, AI-native deal flow must show in revenue acceleration before being credited. Using P/E as the primary IT yardstick (per the sector card), a trailing P/E of 19× sits 14% below the sector floor of 22× and at a 23% discount to the peer median of 24.7× (P38 in sector), screening cheap; forward P/E of 14.4× below trailing implies earnings growth is priced in, but the stock at just 7.5% of its 52-week range with sell-side mean targets -8% below market price signals the market is discounting risks not yet visible in Q1 data. The unresolved critical risk is that Q2FY27 results (filed 2026-10-12, Sep quarter) are not yet extracted — this analysis is one quarter stale precisely when the stock has significantly de-rated, and the unread filing likely contains the catalyst for that weakness.

Titan is India's leading branded jewellery retailer (Tanishq and others), with watches, eyecare and the newly acquired Damas (67% stake) in the Gulf, riding the premiumisation tailwind across about 3,400 stores. In H1 FY27, revenue grew +19.1% YoY to ₹41,970 cr and reported PAT rose +88.6% to ₹4,170 cr (9.9% margin), but that PAT includes a ₹671 cr non-operating fair-value gain on the Damas put option; stripping it gives about ₹3,499 cr (+58% YoY, about 8.3% margin), still strong. Only one half-year period is extracted, so the multi-quarter trajectory cannot be verified. On valuation, trailing P/E is 74× and forward P/E 49×, well above the peer median of about 40× (P76) and EV/EBITDA 48× (P94), though the peer set is mostly autos; the sector card's 60–100× norm for premium franchises is a better yardstick for a 37%-ROE compounder. On that basis we grade it fair, with the upside already priced in. The biggest concern is earnings quality: operating cash flow was about –₹11,177 cr for the half, borrowings rose 2.5× to ₹24,265 cr and inventory climbed to ₹50,861 cr, so profits are not yet converting to cash and the balance sheet is exposed to a gold-price reversal.

fundamental.thesis: Coal India is the state-controlled near-monopoly coal miner that supplies most of India's thermal power fuel, and it earns a steady return from domestic volumes, e-auction premiums and a high dividend payout. Revenue growth accelerated from +9.8% in Q1 to +20.6% (₹54,486 cr), and PAT rose 225.6% to ₹5,359 cr, though the YoY figures use a low, restructured base; PAT margin was flat at about 9.8-9.9%, the 'contracting' signal is distorted by FY26's ₹18,051 cr one-off gain, and EBITDA per tonne fell about 11% QoQ from ₹14,990 to ₹13,329 despite rising 24% YoY. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a steel cyclical, the stock is expensive: the reported 12.6x, or roughly 9x on my estimate using annualised Q2 EBITDA and net debt, is above the 5-8x mid-cycle norm, and the 13.8x trailing P/E and 'cheap vs peers' verdict carry little weight because of the one-off gain and a peer set that includes paint and adhesive companies. fundamental.thesis: Eternal (formerly Zomato) is India's leading food-delivery platform and, through Blinkit, a front-runner in quick commerce, which is now 78.5% of revenue. In H1 FY27, revenue rose 113.7% YoY to ₹44,349 cr and PAT rose 141.1% to ₹217 cr, but growth slowed from +168.5% in FY26 and PAT margin thinned from 0.7% to 0.5%. Using the platform yardstick (EV/sales, growth delivery and unit economics, not the 653x trailing P/E), a 4.2x price/sales for over 100% growth looks fair. However, the stock is the most expensive in its peer set on forward P/E (61x, P100) and EV/EBITDA is about 193x. The biggest risk is sharply falling profit estimates (FY EPS cut 35% in 30 days) while 29 of 32 analysts still rate it a buy, a pattern that often comes before a de-rating. Free cash flow is also negative (H1 FCF ₹-1,378 cr) and the business keeps funding store expansion.

Trent runs Westside, Zudio and Star Bazaar and is one of India's fastest-growing premium-to-value fashion retailers, with same-store sales improving from low single digits in Q4 FY26 to mid-single digits in Q2 FY27. Revenue growth sped up in Q2 FY27 to Rs 5,873 cr, up 24.3% YoY from 18.0% in Q1, but PAT rose only 3.8% to Rs 468 cr. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card uses for premium retailers, the stock trades at 55.3x, the most expensive in its peer group (P100) and 152% above the 21.9x median; trailing P/E of 85.4x is at P88, so valuation is expensive, though inside the card's 60-100x+ range for premium franchises and with forward P/E (55.8x) well below trailing. The biggest risk is that a high multiple meets weak profit growth: if Q2's gap between strong sales and flat profit continues alongside slower inventory turns (4.95x vs 6.11x), the stock is exposed to the 25-40% de-rating the card warns these names suffer on a single guidance reset.

Dabur is a mid-sized Indian FMCG company selling Ayurvedic healthcare, home and personal care, and foods and beverages, with a fast-growing international arm. Growth has picked up from +5.0% in FY26 and +7.3% in Q4FY26 to +10.6% in Q1FY27 and +11.6% in Q2FY27 (Q2 revenue ₹3,563 cr; H1 revenue ₹7,327 cr, +11.1%; H1 PAT ₹1,096 cr, +13.4%). Quality is decent rather than spectacular: domestic volume growth is 5.5% against 10.7% value growth, healthcare grew only 6.9%, and the growth is led by international (+19.4%) and foods (+17.4%). FY26 cash conversion was strong at 1.38x CFO/PAT. On valuation, trailing P/E of 39.4x sits just below the 40-60x FMCG range and at P20 versus household-products peers (forward P/E 31.8x, also P20), but EV/EBITDA of 29.2x is mid-pack at P40, so I grade it cheap only modestly. By the press-release figures, Q2 revenue was ₹45,924 cr and PAT ₹4,650 cr, a margin of about 10.1%, down from 11.3% in Q1. The pre-computed trend signals mix half-year and quarter periods, so I did not rely on them. Using enterprise value to operating profit (EV/EBITDA) plus dividend yield, as the sector card advises for a volume and tariff business, valuation is fair. EV/EBITDA is 11.6x, exactly the peer median, and trailing P/E is 14.65x, at the peer median and just above the 8–14x energy range. P/B is 1.26x against an annualised H1 ROE of about 19%, which looks attractive. The forward P/E of 9.5x depends on FY27 estimates that analysts raised 28% in 30 days while trimming next-year estimates by 3.5%. The biggest risk is that the doubling of profit comes mostly from gas-marketing spreads, which swing with LNG prices and are not structural. That makes FY27 look like a peak year. The newly started Mangalore PTA plant (purified terephthalic acid, a petrochemical) also adds exposure to a segment that is currently losing money.

fundamental.thesis: Canara Bank is a large public sector bank (62.93% GoI ownership) and one of India's top-5 lenders by advances (₹13.6L cr), with a franchise spanning retail, wholesale, and treasury segments; the key yardstick here is P/B vs ROE, per the sector card, not P/E. H1FY27 shows a notable bifurcation: PAT grew strongly +31.3% YoY to ₹10,562 cr on dramatically improved asset quality (Gross NPA 1.33%, Net NPA 0.30%, PCR 95.34%), but total income contracted -3.38% YoY — revenue trajectory has decelerated from +7.7% (FY26) to -3.4% (H1FY27), driven by treasury revenue declining -18% YoY and NIM compression (2.06% FY26 vs 2.51% in Q4FY26), while PAT margin has expanded from 11.7% (FY26) to 13.1% (H1FY27) on sharply lower credit costs. At P/B of 1.02× against ROE of 15.9%, the stock is unambiguously cheap by the sector card's prescribed lender yardstick — sector card benchmark is P/B < 1.5 with ROE > 12% = cheap — and sits at P0 (cheapest) in its 14-peer regional bank cohort on both trailing P/E (6.1×, -64% vs median 16.8×) and forward P/E (5.7×), though much of this structural discount is explained by PSU overhang and below-median CASA (29.86% vs private sector ~40%+). The single biggest risk is NIM pressure persisting through the deposit repricing cycle — NIM at 2.06% for FY26 is already thin for a PSU bank and any further compression from EBLR-linked loan repricing faster than deposit cost decline would erode the PAT margin expansion thesis and keep revenue growth negative.

fundamental.thesis: Punjab National Bank is India's second-largest public-sector lender, with ₹13.4 lakh crore of advances that grew 14.7% YoY, led by MSME (+19.8%) and overseas loans (+62.7%). In Q2 FY27, total income rose 5.4% YoY to ₹38,185 cr and net profit rose 12.8% to ₹5,532 cr; asset quality keeps improving, with Gross NPA down from 3.19% to 2.95% to 2.55%, Net NPA at 0.25%, slippage at 0.77% and provision coverage at 97%, though the revenue trend is noisy because one period row looks inconsistent. Using the lender yardstick of price-to-book against ROE, the stock trades at 0.83x book against a 13% TTM ROE (17.3% in the latest quarter), which is about 44% below the regional-bank median P/B of 1.5x and in the bottom 15% of peers, so it grades as cheap; the trailing P/E of 6.75x is consistent with that but is not the main yardstick. The main concern is funding: cost of deposits rose from 2.50% to 2.74% YoY, CASA slipped from 37.0% to 36.6%, domestic deposits grew only 9.5% against 12.5% domestic loan growth, and treasury income fell 57%, all of which could cap the 2.6–2.7% margin guidance.

fundamental.thesis: IDFC First Bank is a mid-sized private bank with a retail-heavy loan book and a strong deposit franchise (CASA 48.4%), now scaling fast after years of rebuilding profitability. In Q2FY27, PAT was ₹1,045 cr, up 196.5% YoY off a depressed base and above ₹1,000 cr for a second straight quarter. Loans grew 30.1% YoY (22.2% excluding FCNR(B)-backed loans, up from 20.6% in Q1), deposits grew 25.9%, and asset quality kept improving: net NPA fell from 0.48% to 0.44% to 0.40%, and gross NPA was 1.32% vs 1.61% at FY26-end. Valuation is graded on P/B plus ROE, as the sector card requires for lenders, not on trailing P/E: P/B is 1.31x (P36 among peers, 11% below the 1.5x median) against annualised ROE of only 10.6%, which is below the 12% bar for 'cheap', so the stock is fair. The 38x trailing P/E is distorted by weak FY26 earnings (PAT ₹1,611 cr), and the 11x forward P/E sits exactly at the peer median. The main risk is that rapid growth is outpacing the bank's profitability engine: CASA slipped from 50.8% to 48.4% and NIM was diluted by FCNR(B) funding, Q2 ROA fell to 0.93% from 1.06%, and capital adequacy (CAR) dropped to 15.05% from 15.6% while the loan book grows about 30%.

H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,760 cr (+10.2% YoY) and PAT was Rs 1,140 cr (+65.1%), but subtracting Q1 implies a more ordinary Q2 of about Rs 891 cr revenue (about +10.5%) and Rs 384 cr PAT (about +11%, about 43% margin), so the 'expanding' margin signal looks distorted by Q1's unusually high 87% margin, likely including non-operating gains, and by FY26 figures that appear understated about 10x; recruitment billings also slowed from about 17% in Q1 (implied) to 12.6% in Q2, though management cites timing effects and puts underlying growth at 14-15%, while 99acres billings accelerated to +21.2%. Using EV/EBITDA and growth delivery as the platform yardstick, I grade valuation fair: EV/EBITDA of 53.0x is 10% above the peer median (P78), while the 44.7x trailing P/E (P22) may be flattered by non-operating income and the 1.33x P/B (P0) looks less meaningful with ROE at just 4.6%; the stock sits near its 52-week low, but the price basis needs checking because the 14.4% range position implies about Rs 1,000 while the consensus upside implies about Rs 1,180, and the 146% dividend yield is clearly bad data. The biggest risk is that recruitment billings stay near or below the 12.6% Q2 pace rather than returning to management's 14-15% underlying estimate, which would undermine the multiple in a risk-off market where crude and sector positioning are also headwinds.

Marico is a leading Indian FMCG company built on Parachute coconut oil, Saffola and value-added hair oils, with growing foods, digital-first and international businesses (international was about 24% of FY26 revenue); 96% of its business is gaining or holding market share. The extracted Q2FY27 figures show consolidated revenue of ₹2,722 cr, up 8.4% YoY, and PAT of ₹683 cr, up 71.6%, giving a 25.1% margin, or ₹550 cr and about 20.2% on a parent-attributable basis. Revenue growth has slowed sharply from about +20-23% in Q1FY27/FY26 to +8.4%, and the profit jump comes after exceptional items that were not broken out, so the margin expansion should not be treated as recurring. These Q2 figures also conflict with yfinance (₹2,022 cr revenue) and with the extracted Q1 base of ₹3,957 cr, so the quarter's size and the slowdown need checking against the full results PDF. On valuation, the trailing P/E of 59.4x is at the top of the 40-60x FMCG range. Marico is also the priciest of its peers (P100) on trailing P/E, forward P/E and EV/EBITDA, sitting 35-42% above the peer medians, at 80% of its 52-week range. The forward P/E of 42.9x does price in growth, so I grade it expensive: a premium multiple meeting slowing top-line growth is the main risk.

fundamental.thesis: Indian Hotels (IHCL) runs India's largest hotel chain, with Taj and other brands across 670 hotels including 280 in the pipeline. It earns more and more from asset-light management fees, which grew 25% YoY in Q2, and it is still early in a RevPAR (revenue per available room) upcycle, up 25% YoY in Q2 and 28% for full-service hotels. Q2FY27 revenue rose 21.0% YoY to ₹2,566 cr, up from +14.6% in Q1FY27. PAT rose 23.0% to ₹349 cr. Management raised full-year revenue guidance from 12-14% to 15-17%, and H1 cash conversion was strong (CFO/PAT 1.27x, FCF ₹546 cr). The 'contracting' margin signal mostly reflects comparing a seasonally weak Q2 against full-year figures: on a same-quarter basis the EBITDA margin (30.7%) and PAT margin (13.6%) are roughly flat to slightly up YoY. On valuation, hotels are capital-intensive, so I used EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick. At 28.2x, IHCL sits around the 61st percentile of its sector, with a trailing P/E of 44.5x (P59) and a forward P/E of 35.6x. That is fair, not cheap, for 20%+ earnings growth, and the stock sits at 38.5% of its 52-week range. Note that the snapshot's 49% dividend yield and 18.99 debt/equity look like data-unit errors, given ₹4,369 cr of gross cash. The biggest risk is that a premium-multiple discretionary stock gets de-rated in a risk-off market with crude above $100, which could squeeze travel and MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences and events) demand even while operating numbers stay strong.

fundamental.thesis: Colgate-Palmolive India is the dominant oral-care franchise, with the number one toothpaste brand at roughly three times the size of the second player, 69-70% gross margins and an 81.6% ROE. Revenue growth has picked up from flat in FY26 to +9.0% in Q4FY26 and about +12% for the last two quarters, reaching Rs 1,706 cr (+12.4% YoY) in Q2FY27 on high-single-digit toothpaste volume growth, but PAT growth slowed from +10.6% to +4.3% (Rs 342 cr). PAT margin fell from 22.3% to 20.0% and EBITDA margin from 32.2% to 29.0% because ad spend rose 39.8% YoY to 18.4% of sales, while gross margin held flat. On the FMCG yardstick of P/E cross-checked with EV/EBITDA, trailing P/E of 41.1x sits at the low end of the 40-60x sector band and 6% below the peer median of 43.8x (P40), EV/EBITDA of 28.3x is at P20, and forward P/E of 34.1x implies earnings growth, so the stock grades fair with the price at 33% of its 52-week range. Muthoot Finance is India's largest gold-loan NBFC, with very high profitability: annualised ROE of about 29% and ROA of about 5.4% in H1 FY27, and NIM of 10.4% in Q1 FY27. Growth is strong but slowing. Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 8,695 cr (+34.5% YoY) and PAT was Rs 2,825 cr (+43.1% YoY), and AUM growth has eased from about 50% to 43% YoY over the last four periods. PAT margin has slipped from 36.2% in 9M FY26 to 32.5% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY27 PAT of Rs 6,046 cr implies Q2 PAT of about Rs 3,221 cr, but YoY growth for Q2 cannot be computed from the data given. Using the lender yardstick (P/B against sustainable ROE), P/B of 3.0x sits exactly at the peer median (P44) while ROE of about 30% is well above most peers, and trailing P/E of 11.2x is in the cheapest quartile of peers (P22, 44% below the 20.1x median), so the stock is fair, leaning cheap. The biggest risk is that this ROE is boosted by a historically high gold price, now at $4,075/oz and falling. On top of that come a reported gross NPA jump from 0.14% to about 2.3%, a CGST Section 67 tax search disclosed on 2026-11-02, and several data inconsistencies.

fundamental.thesis: Polycab is India's largest wires and cables maker, with about 30-31% share of the organised market. It is scaling a consumer electricals (FMEG) business and a smaller EPC arm, and has net cash of ₹4,520cr and an 11-day working-capital cycle. Revenue growth sped up from +39% YoY in Q1 FY27 to +53% in Q2 FY27 (₹9,900cr), and PAT rose 43% to ₹990cr. PAT margin edged up to 10.0% from 9.4% in FY26. FMEG grew 124% and posted its first double-digit EBIT margin (10.1%). Much of the headline growth is copper price pass-through, though: copper rose 40-45% in H1, while wire volumes grew only 10.5% and cable volumes about 5%. Underlying demand is healthy but well below the +53% headline. I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, which suits this capital-intensive business. At 35.0x it sits close to the sector peer median of 34.0x (P53). Trailing P/E is 53.8x (P50) and forward P/E is 38.5x, which points to expected earnings growth. On the sector card's 50-80x range for electricals this is fair, not cheap, and the stock is at 99.8% of its 52-week range. The main risk is that copper-inflated revenue and record margins revert as commodity prices normalise or UltraTech's entry into wires squeezes pricing. That risk is larger because, in a risk-off market, a stock priced for perfection can lose 30-50% of its valuation multiple quickly.

On the lender yardstick (price-to-book against return on equity, not P/E), the stock is fair rather than cheap: a P/B of 2.8x against an ROE of about 15–15.8% is a reasonable price for a well-capitalised lender (CRAR 42%) that benefits from rate cuts. The 19.6x P/E looks 'cheap vs peers' only because it is compared against the whole market, not other housing lenders. The main thing to watch is asset quality: gross NPA rose from 1.08% at FY26 to 1.35%, even though it is still 8bps better year-on-year, and the bad-loan provision cover is thin at about 34.5%.

Using P/B plus ROE, the right yardstick for a lender, valuation is fair: P/B of 1.63x sits just above the 1.5x cheap threshold despite 16.5% TTM ROE (the bank reports 24.58%), trailing P/E of 11.03x is not the basis for the grade, the 'cheap vs peers' rank is against the broad market rather than banks, and the 36.51x forward P/E conflicts with recent earnings and needs checking, though being 15.7% up the 52-week range offers a better entry point. fundamental.thesis: IRFC is the Government of India's dedicated financing arm for Indian Railways (82.9% government-owned after the June 2026 OFS). It mainly leases rolling stock and project assets to the Ministry of Railways, so credit risk is quasi-sovereign and gross and net NPA have been 0.0% for every reported period. Revenue is growing fast and the pace is picking up: up 22.8% YoY to ₹16,316 cr in H1FY27, against +0.5% in FY26 and -2.4% in 9M FY26. Implied Q2 revenue is about ₹8,055 cr (+26% YoY). Profit is not keeping pace, though. H1 PAT rose only 10.3% to ₹3,886 cr, the PAT margin slipped from 26.5% to 23.8%, and NIM eased from 1.55% to 1.48%, so earnings are rising more slowly than the loan book. I graded valuation on P/B against ROE, which is the right yardstick for a lender, not P/E. At 2.3x book for a 12.8–13.3% ROE and roughly 1.4% ROA, the stock is fair, maybe slightly full, for a low-margin, policy-driven financier. The 'cheap' peer reading (trailing P/E 18.7x, P20) compares IRFC with the whole market rather than with lenders, so I don't rely on it. The biggest risk is that further government stake sales add share supply while thin, shrinking spreads keep EPS growth near 10% even with strong loan growth.

The lender yardstick in the sector card does not fit an exchange, so I graded valuation on P/E and EV/EBITDA against growth: trailing P/E is 53.9x, about 53% above the broad-market median of 35.2x (P73), forward P/E is 33.6x, EV/EBITDA is 39.3x (P81), and P/B is 17.0x, backed by a 37.9% ROE and debt/equity of 0.11, so the stock looks fair for a high-return, near-monopoly franchise but leaves little margin of safety. fundamental.thesis: NIACL is India's largest PSU general insurer (85.44% government-owned), writing motor, health, marine, and fire coverage domestically and internationally, with a regulatory solvency ratio of 1.80×; however, the franchise is structurally loss-making at the underwriting level and profits depend entirely on investment income. Using P/B + ROE as the correct yardstick for an insurer (not P/E), P/B of 0.76× ranks NIACL at P1 in the broad peer set and appears cheap on its face, but a TTM ROE of only 3.4% fully explains this discount — it is structural cheapness, not mispricing — and analyst EPS estimates have been cut –47% in just 30 days, a classic pre-derating signal that the forward P/E of 9.2× bakes in recovery assumptions the combined-ratio trend does not yet support. The dominant near-term risk is a qualified audit conclusion on unreconciled reinsurance recoverable balances (₹75,490L gross, ₹13,783L doubtful-debt provision), compounded by a new CMD appointment in September 2026 and a mandatory Ind AS accounting transition due April 2027, leaving both governance and accounting transparency materially unresolved.

Niva Bupa is a standalone health insurer with about 11% share of India's retail health market and 27 million lives covered, growing through agents (270,000, up from 250,000 last quarter), branches, banca partners and a direct channel growing 46% YoY. Growth has picked up: Q2FY27 gross written premium rose 35% YoY to Rs 2,484 cr (Q1FY27: +32%), retail health premium rose 47%, and H1FY27 PAT more than doubled (+107%) to Rs 273 cr. On valuation I used price-to-book against return on equity, with forward P/E as a cross-check, because the trailing P/E of 75x is distorted by a weak FY26 and the Ind-AS transition. fundamental.thesis: Blue Dart Express is India's dominant integrated express logistics company and a DHL Group subsidiary, operating time-definite air and ground freight networks with significant pricing power in the premium segment. Q1FY27 showed a sharp positive inflection: revenue grew +15.0% YoY to ₹1,658 crore (accelerating from a flat +7% range across all FY26 quarters), while PAT surged 81.2% YoY to ₹88 crore with EBITDA margin expanding to 16.7% — the operating-leverage story is finally showing up in PAT. Using EV/EBITDA as the preferred yardstick for capital-intensive logistics (EV/EBITDA is unavailable in the snapshot), the fallback trailing P/E of 40.4× sits within the Industrials sector range of 28–45× (fair), but forward P/E at 26.5× — below the 28× lower bound — implies the market is pricing in substantial earnings growth; the stock at 10.6% of its 52-week range (near ₹4,883 vs a 52-week high of ₹7,036) at a fair-to-cheap forward multiple presents a potentially asymmetric setup, though the falling-knife risk at this proximity to the low demands caution. The single biggest fundamental risk is that crude oil at $89.72 and rising directly compresses unit economics since freight and handling costs constitute 58% of revenues, and the 90-day EPS revision of -24.3% signals the sell side is already cutting numbers — a classic pre-derating pattern that could undermine the inflection narrative.

Cemindia Projects (formerly ITD Cementation, now Adani-group promoted) is a mid-cap EPC contractor for marine, metro, tunnel and foundation projects, and it carries a record order book of ₹32,715 cr as of Sep-26, up about 58% from ₹20,646 cr a year earlier and roughly 3x trailing revenue. Revenue growth has picked up sharply: from +5.6% YoY in Q1FY27 to +25.2% in Q2FY27 (₹2,749 cr, derived as H1 ₹5,470 cr minus Q1 ₹2,721 cr), with Q2 PAT up 21.3% to about ₹131 cr. Profitability has not kept pace, however: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 10.2% from 11.1%, PAT margin is under 5%, and H1 operating cash flow turned negative (CFO/PAT -0.29x, FCF -₹281 cr) because of a ₹474 cr build in contract assets. Using EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for an order-book business, the stock trades at 19.9x versus a broad-market median of 23.3x, and its trailing P/E of 34.3x sits inside the 28–45x Industrials band, so I grade it fair; with the stock at 91% of its 52-week range and sell-side EPS estimates cut 7.9% over 90 days, near-term upside looks limited even though the order book gives good revenue visibility.

fundamental.thesis: CONCOR is India's dominant rail container logistics PSU (~70% share in rail containerisation), operating EXIM and domestic freight corridors with an embedded structural role in India's trade infrastructure. Revenue growth decelerated to near-zero in Q1FY27 (+0.3% YoY on ₹2,160 cr) continuing a multi-quarter stagnation (Q1FY26: +2.4%, FY25: +2.7%), with PAT essentially flat at +0.1% YoY and EBITDA/PAT margins contracting to 24.5%/12.3% from their 9M FY26 peaks of 26.4%/14.4% — the Domestic segment is structurally weak at a 4.14% PBIT margin and -3.5% volume decline. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive logistics infrastructure business, CONCOR trades at 14.2× — a 39% discount to the broad-market median of 23.3× (P23 percentile), with trailing P/E of 28.5× at the lower bound of the Industrials sector range (28–45×), grading as fair rather than cheap because ROE of 9.8% (below cost of equity) and a very high D/E of 7.39 undermine the P/B multiple case. The single biggest risk is management's bullish FY27 guidance (18% overall growth driven by DFC-JNPA connectivity and assured transit trains) having zero support from Q1 execution, compounded by an unquantified Land License Fee liability with Railways and a governance non-compliance flag (only 1 independent director as of June 2026), both of which create PSU-specific overhang that sell-side estimate cuts (-9.2% in 30 days, -10.5% in 90 days) are beginning to price in.

Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% YoY to ₹639 cr and PAT was about ₹97 cr (15.2% margin, about +10% YoY against ₹88 cr). On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital goods, the stock trades at 20.0×, about 14% below the broad-market median, and its trailing P/E of 40.2× sits inside the 28–45× industrials range, so it grades fair rather than cheap. Elgi Equipments is a mid-cap Indian air-compressor maker with a global footprint (26 subsidiaries; about 51% of revenue from outside India), and compressors make up about 92% of sales. H1 FY27 revenue grew 19.7% YoY to ₹2,196 cr and PAT grew 11.9% to ₹232 cr. Netting out Q1 (₹1,062 cr / ₹103 cr) implies Q2 revenue of about ₹1,134 cr (+17% YoY) and PAT of about ₹129 cr (+6% YoY), so growth has cooled from +22.5% in Q1 and profit is lagging sales, partly due to ₹11 cr of restructuring charges. Earnings are cash-backed (CFO/PAT 1.05x, H1 free cash flow ₹166 cr, net cash), and annualised ROE is about 19-21%. On valuation, trailing P/E of 44.3x sits at the top of the 28-45x Industrials band and EV/EBITDA of 32x is about 37% above the broad-market median, so I grade it fair but stretched (P64-P75 vs peers, stock at 86% of its 52-week range); the forward P/E of 33x already assumes faster earnings growth. The biggest risk is that PAT growth keeps lagging revenue while the stock is priced near its highs, which leaves little room for a miss.

fundamental.thesis: Emmvee is an integrated solar module and cell maker with 10.3 GW of installed module capacity, 2.94 GW of TOPCon cell capacity and an order book of 10.4 GW. It is tagged Industrials/IT in our data, but it really trades on the solar-manufacturing cycle. In H1 FY27, revenue rose 45.1% YoY to ₹3,132 cr and PAT rose 79.1% to ₹762 cr, a 24.3% PAT margin. Growth is clearly slowing from the +116% revenue growth of FY26. EBITDA margin is flat at around 35%, and new orders in Q2 were only 1.5 GW against 10.3 GW of module capacity running at 44% utilisation. No separate quarterly breakdown was available, so these are half-year figures. On the yardstick for capital-intensive businesses, it looks cheap: EV/EBITDA is 13.4x (P21, 42% below the broad-market median of 23.3x), trailing P/E is 19.5x (below the 28–45x Industrials range) and forward P/E is 13.7x. That multiple is being applied to what look like peak-cycle 35% EBITDA margins, and the stock is already at 90% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is earnings quality. Cash from operations covered only 0.54x of PAT in H1 and 0.18x in FY26, free cash flow in FY26 was -₹453 cr, and analysts have cut next-year EPS estimates by 12.5% in the last 30 days. Together these suggest margins may fall back as module supply catches up.

fundamental.thesis: Siemens Energy India (ENRIN) is a newly-listed (June 2025) power equipment company demerged from Siemens Limited, serving India's electrification build-out across power transmission (55.8% of revenue) and power generation (44.2%) — a structurally well-positioned business but with less than 18 months of standalone track record. Official 9M FY26 filings show revenue of ₹6,791 cr (+31.1% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,128 cr (+52.2%, 16.6% margin) with operating margins expanding 260 bps — a genuinely strong growth print — but three signals undercut the quality: (a) book-to-revenue declining from 2.25× (Q1) to 1.18× (H1), indicating execution outpacing new order wins; (b) Q2 CFO/PAT of just 0.09×, signalling earnings are not converting to cash; and (c) Power Transmission order backlog flat/down (-3.2% YoY) despite the headline growth. The stock is priced for prolonged flawless execution at peak cycle, and high financial leverage (D/E 4.48×) leaves no balance-sheet buffer if order inflows slow or margins disappoint.

Finolex Cables is an established Indian maker of electrical wires and cables (about 88% of revenue) and optical fibre cables (about 9%), with a 4 million fibre-km draw facility being expanded and a small EHV cable joint venture. Revenue growth has accelerated sharply from +5.0% YoY in Q2FY26 to +19.0% in Q4FY26 and +44.2% in Q1FY27 (Rs 2,013 cr, PAT Rs 249 cr, +53.1%), and an unlabeled latest row of Rs 2,269 cr revenue and Rs 286 cr PAT is probably Q2FY27 but is not confirmed. Much of this growth is copper-driven price pass-through rather than real demand: there were 14 price hikes in FY26 (about +24.5% effective) while electrical wire volumes grew only about 7%. Other income (Rs 237 cr in FY26) also flatters PAT, so the headline growth overstates the underlying business momentum. On valuation, trailing P/E of 24.8x sits below the 28-45x Industrials band, but EV/EBITDA of 22.8x is right at the market median (P49), so I grade it fair on EV/EBITDA, which suits a capex-heavy, other-income-heavy business. The stock is at 94.6% of its 52-week range, which leaves little cushion, and the biggest risk is that a copper price reversal or project-segment slowdown exposes weak volume growth and compresses reported revenue and margins.

Great Eastern Shipping is India's largest private-sector shipping company, running crude/product tankers, gas carriers and dry-bulk vessels plus an offshore-services arm. It is a cyclical, asset-heavy business, so the Industrials order-book framing does not fit well. H1FY27 revenue rose 56.8% YoY to ₹3,830 cr and PAT rose 137.4% to ₹2,578 cr, a 57.0% PAT margin. That is a sharp turn from -14.7% revenue growth in H1FY26, but Q2-alone growth cannot be isolated. The implied Q2 figures (revenue about ₹1,825 cr, PAT about ₹1,269 cr, and an EBITDA margin near 97% derived from the H1 and Q1 rows) look inflated, which points to vessel-sale gains or other one-offs that should not be extrapolated. On EV/EBITDA (4.7x) and P/B with ROE (1.19x, 18.8%), the right yardsticks for capital-intensive shipping, the stock is cheap: P2–P6 versus the broad market, with a net-cash balance sheet (filing net debt/equity -0.45, interest cover 84x). However, forward P/E (7.2x) above trailing (6.9x) says the market is pricing these as near-peak earnings. The biggest risk is a turn in freight rates: shipping earnings can halve within a few quarters, and a single-digit P/E on peak-cycle profits is often a value trap rather than a mispricing.

fundamental.thesis: GRSE is India's premier PSU defence shipbuilder with a ₹50,000 cr order book (~7× FY26 revenues of ₹7,002 cr), providing exceptional multi-year revenue visibility backed by the government's defence indigenisation drive and growing capital procurement allocations. Q1FY27 revenue grew 38.5% YoY to ₹1,815 cr and PAT grew 43.8% YoY to ₹173 cr, sustaining a consistently strong 30–49% growth pattern across 6 periods, though EBITDA margins have contracted from 14.9% (FY25) to 13.7% (Q1FY27) and guidance has only been 'maintained' twice — no upgrades despite the execution strength. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive shipbuilder, 29.34× sits within the 28–45× Industrials range but at P65 vs the broad market, rendering valuation fair; the forward P/E of 27.33× at a meaningful discount to trailing 34.84× confirms analysts expect continued EPS growth, while the P/B of 10.59× (P84 vs peers) signals the PSU defence franchise premium is already well-embedded at current prices. The critical risk is severely negative cash conversion — CFO/PAT was –0.39× in FY26 and –2.21× in H1FY26 — driven by trade receivables turnover collapsing from 17.91× to 6.27×, indicating government client payment delays that are building acute working capital stress and could erode the currently pristine near-zero debt balance sheet if collections do not normalise.

HBL Engineering is a midcap maker of industrial and defence/aviation batteries and an electronics business (its largest growth engine in FY26), with a net-cash balance sheet (₹274 cr net cash, only ₹5.8 cr borrowings) and ROCE of 32.9%. Growth has sharply reversed: revenue went from +75-81% in FY26 to +6.0% in Q1FY27 and -17.3% in H1FY27 (₹1,510 cr vs ₹1,825 cr). PAT fell 43.1% to ₹302 cr, PAT margin dropped from 29.1% to 20.0%, and EBITDA margin from 42.3% to 25.8%. The decline is driven by Electronics, down 39.4% to ₹591 cr; batteries grew modestly (Industrial +7.5%, Defence +16.4%). Implied Q2 alone (H1 minus Q1) looks worse, at roughly -29% revenue YoY, but that figure is derived rather than separately reported. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick: 19.3x is about 17% below the broad-market median of 23.3x, and trailing P/E of 27.3x sits just under the 28-45x Industrials band. Because that trailing earnings base is still shrinking and no order-book, forward P/E or guidance data is available, I grade it fair rather than cheap. The biggest risk is earnings quality and visibility: H1 operating cash flow was roughly zero (CFO/PAT -0.01x vs 0.91x in FY26), and without order-book data there is no evidence the Electronics slump has bottomed.

Hindustan Copper is India's only vertically integrated copper miner. It is a state-owned price-taker whose earnings move mainly with global copper prices and its own ore output, with the Malanjkhand mine as the core asset. On comparable quarters, growth has sharply accelerated: revenue rose from +4.6% YoY in Q1FY26 to +109.7% in Q3FY26 and +81.4% in Q1FY27 (Rs 936 cr), and PAT jumped 162.5% to Rs 352 cr as PAT margin widened from 26.0% to 37.6% and EBITDA margin reached 56%. That points to strong operating leverage on copper prices, though FY26 free cash flow was negative (Rs -182 cr, CFO/PAT 0.76x) and FY26 included a Rs 96 cr one-off gain. As a commodity cyclical, the right yardstick is EV/EBITDA, and at 33.4x it is far above the 5-8x mid-cycle range for cyclicals, at the 70th percentile of the broad market, and backed by a P/B of 14.8x (92nd percentile). The 25.6x forward P/E already prices in continued strong copper prices, so we grade it expensive even after allowing for the 30.6% ROE. The biggest near-term risk is the Q2FY27 results on 11 Nov 2026, two days away, where any normalisation in copper realisations or output would hit a stock priced for peak-cycle earnings.

PAT fell about 8% from Q1, and PAT margin eased from 37.8% to about 33.9%. On the dossier's yardstick for cyclicals (EV/EBITDA), 7.4× sits at the top of the 5–8× mid-cycle band, and it is being applied to near-peak EBITDA margins of about 50%. So the stock is fair rather than cheap, even though the 11× trailing P/E and the P5–P8 broad-market peer ranks look optimistic, partly because there are no tight aluminium peers to compare against. The biggest risk is that this record half-year comes from high aluminium prices on the LME (London Metal Exchange) and strong alumina realisations; a falling commodity price would reverse earnings quickly, while the alumina/chemicals segment is already down 5.75% YoY.

fundamental.thesis: Navin Fluorine is an Indian fluorochemicals maker in refrigerant gases (HFC/R32), specialty chemicals and contract manufacturing (CDMO), and is adding 15,000 MTPA of R32-equivalent capacity on the back of the China+1 shift. Revenue growth has held at roughly +41% to +51% YoY for six periods: H1FY27 revenue was ₹2,236 cr (+50.7%) and PAT was ₹513 cr (+93%). The implied Q2FY27 is about ₹1,191 cr revenue (+57% YoY vs ₹758 cr) and ₹270 cr PAT (+82%), and EBITDA margin rose to 33.7% from 28.6% a year ago, though cash conversion slipped to 0.89x CFO/PAT as receivables grew. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive chemicals business, the stock trades at 34.6× against 5–8× for mid-cycle chemical cyclicals, alongside 56× trailing P/E, 38.8× forward P/E and around P75–P79 across all four peer metrics; with the price at 93% of its 52-week range, it is expensive even after strong upward EPS revisions (+22.6% over 90 days). The biggest risk is that refrigerant-gas prices come off their cycle high while ₹319 cr of half-year capex and ₹1,070 cr of net debt are still ramping, which would squeeze margins on a valuation that leaves no room for a miss.

NMDC is India's largest iron-ore miner, a state-owned company that sells into a protected domestic steel upcycle but takes global ore prices as given. Revenue growth has slowed sharply, from +27.0% in H1FY26 and +33.3% for FY26 to just +0.8% in Q1FY27 (₹6,795 cr). Margins carried the quarter: PAT was ₹1,976 cr (+0.4% YoY, 29.1% margin) and EBITDA margin rose to 46.9% from 38.4% a year earlier. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive commodity producer, the stock trades at 7.8×, which is the top of the 5–8× mid-cycle cyclical range, so it is fair rather than cheap, even though trailing P/E of 10.45× (forward 8.8×) sits below the 12–22× Materials band. The broad-market peer ranking is not a like-for-like comparison and should not be read as a cheap signal. The biggest risk is the Karnataka Mineral Tax Bill: its ₹15,786 cr contingent liability is about 20% of market cap and about two years of PAT, and on top of that roughly ₹11,000 cr is owed by the stressed state-linked buyers NMDC Steel and RINL.

fundamental.thesis: Paradeep Phosphates is a mid-sized Indian phosphatic and complex fertiliser maker (about 3.7 MT capacity running near full utilisation, 18 states, around 12 mn farmers). It is a commodity-spread business exposed to sulphur, ammonia and phosphoric-acid costs and to government subsidy timing, so it should be judged on EBITDA per tonne rather than on volume. Q2FY27 revenue grew only +7% YoY to ₹7,364 cr, slowing sharply from +49% in Q2FY26 and +36% in Q1FY27, while PAT fell 64% YoY to ₹122 cr and PAT margin compressed from 5.0% to 1.7%; EBITDA margin halved from 10.2% to 5.8% on sulphur cost and availability pressure. On the capital-intensive yardstick, EV/EBITDA of 9.9x is above the card's 5–8x mid-cycle range for chemical cyclicals, while trailing P/E of 15.3x sits inside the 12–22x Materials band; I grade it fair, not cheap. The 'cheap vs peers' signal comes from a broad-market comparison with no fertiliser peers, and the trailing multiple is flattered by earlier high-margin quarters while FY EPS estimates were cut about 28% in 30 days. The biggest risk is that the margin squeeze persists while working capital balloons: H1FY27 free cash flow was -₹2,625 cr with CFO/PAT of -4.5x, likely from subsidy receivables and inventory build, on a balance sheet with roughly 1x debt/equity.

fundamental.thesis: Sarda Energy and Minerals is a midcap integrated steel, ferro-alloys and power producer, with power as the largest profit driver (H1 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,739 cr at a 51% segment margin). Revenue growth has slowed sharply, from +51.6% in H1 FY26 to -3.2% in H1 FY27 (Rs 3,061 cr), partly against a high base; subtracting Q1 from H1 implies Q2 FY27 revenue of about Rs 1,453 cr (-4.9% YoY) and PAT of about Rs 287 cr (-11% YoY), though the H1 EBITDA margin rose to 43.3% from 40.4% and PAT was about flat (+0.8%). Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick, I grade valuation as fair: 10.5x is above the 5-8x mid-cycle norm for steel cyclicals, which the high-margin power business partly justifies, while the 16.6x trailing P/E sits inside the 12-22x sector range; the 'cheap' peer verdict compares against the broad market rather than close peers, and the 11.0x forward P/E implies about 50% earnings growth that recent results do not yet show. The biggest risk is that earnings stay flat or fall if power weakens further (implied Q2 power revenue about -13% YoY, partly seasonal hydro) while steel stays soft, although the balance sheet looks manageable with net debt of about 0.9x EBITDA, H1 operating cash flow of Rs 981 cr, and the snapshot's 35.2 debt/equity most likely meaning 0.35x rather than very high leverage.

Acutaas Chemicals (formerly Ami Organics) is a midcap maker of pharmaceutical intermediates and CDMO services that is now adding semiconductor-grade specialty chemicals, with a new South Korea plant inaugurated ahead of schedule. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42.7% YoY to about ₹437 cr and PAT rose 71.4% to about ₹123 cr, lifting the PAT margin to 28.2% and the EBITDA margin to 40.3%. Growth eased from +59.1% in Q1 FY27 but is still roughly in line with the +43.0% of Q3 FY26, and management raised FY27 guidance to about 30% revenue growth and a 38-40% EBITDA margin. Earnings appear cash-backed, with H1 CFO/PAT at 1.11x and FCF of ₹92 cr, and the automated 'decelerating' signal is unreliable because the FY26 row (₹134 cr revenue) and the duplicate Q1 rows look like extraction errors. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for this capital-intensive CDMO/chemicals business, the stock is clearly expensive at 50.8x, versus a broad-market median of 23.3x (P89). Its trailing P/E of 89.5x and P/B of 15.5x are also near the top of the market, and it trades at 87% of its 52-week range, about 3.6% above the mean analyst target. The biggest risk is that this valuation already prices in flawless delivery on an aggressive capex and CDMO ramp, which leaves little room if margins slip or the shrinking specialty chemicals segment (-20% YoY) drags further.

The main risks are that net debt has risen to ₹1,317 cr after the ₹2,077 cr Gennova minority buyout, and gross margin has slipped from 61.3% to 59% even as headline margins improve.

fundamental.thesis: GLAXO is the Indian subsidiary of GlaxoSmithKline, a premium MNC branded-formulations franchise with 22–27% market shares in general medicines and vaccines respectively, operating entirely within India's domestic market with zero US generics exposure and no tariff risk from recent US pharma levies. Q1FY27 revenue accelerated sharply to +16.56% YoY (₹938 cr vs ₹805 cr in Q1FY26), a marked re-acceleration from near-stagnation at +1.9% through FY26 and -1.2% in Q1FY26, driven by Shingrix (+65% growth), vaccines therapy (+18.5%), cardiac (+16.9%), and anti-diabetic (+17.3%) segments — PAT grew 15.68% YoY to ₹237 cr but PAT margin contracted to 25.3% from 27.1% in FY26 as S&A normalises, with management guiding EBITDA margins to settle at ~34% vs the 36-38% range seen over FY26. At a trailing P/E of 44.85× (above the 28–40× pharma sector benchmark), forward P/E of 35.72× (within range, confirming near-term earnings growth priced in), and EV/EBITDA of 33.98× (P71 vs broad market), GLAXO grades as fair — the premium is defensible for a defensive, India-only, brand-led franchise with no binary US/FDA risk, but peer rank at P65 on trailing P/E confirms there is no meaningful discount on offer. The principal risk is that the guided margin normalisation to ~34% EBITDA compresses PAT margins further if the current revenue acceleration fades back toward the guided 8–10% established-business growth range, making the present fair multiple vulnerable.

Valuation is fair on the pharma P/E yardstick: trailing P/E of 33.4x sits inside the 28–40x sector range, forward P/E is 22.6x, EV/EBITDA is 18.0x (P35 vs a broad-market peer set), and P/B is 4.4x. fundamental.thesis: Indegene sells outsourced commercial, medical and regulatory content and technology services to global pharma companies, and it is a services business rather than a drug maker, with US revenue about 74% of the Q2 FY27 total (₹836 cr of ₹1,122 cr). fundamental.thesis: Dr. Lal Path Labs is India's leading organised pathology diagnostics network — 300+ labs and ~2,000 collection centres — serving a structurally underpenetrated preventive-testing market with no US tariff exposure (pure domestic revenue). Q1FY27 revenue grew 19.1% YoY to ₹798 cr, accelerating sharply from the 10.6–10.7% band seen in Q2–Q3FY26; PAT grew faster at 28% YoY to ₹170 cr with EBITDA margin expanding to 35.0% (from a prior-quarter range of 26.6–30.7%), confirming that operating leverage is kicking in as volume scales over a relatively fixed cost base. At a trailing P/E of 59.2× against the Healthcare sector benchmark of 28–40× (pharma), and sitting at P77–P89 versus 473 broad-market peers on every major multiple, the stock is unambiguously expensive — the forward P/E of 43.85× shows the market has already priced in a robust earnings catch-up, and at 88.8% of its 52-week range there is minimal margin of safety. The single biggest risk is the ₹380 cr acquisition of Sunshine Healthcare in Ghana (a frontier market) via a Dubai subsidiary, which introduces material execution, currency, and governance complexity at exactly the point where a stretched valuation tolerates no negative surprises.

Global Health (Medanta) runs multi-specialty tertiary hospitals across 6 locations (Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna, Noida, Ranchi, Indore) with 3,811 beds, and is expanding in NCR through a ₹997 cr, 500-bed Ghaziabad project. H1 FY27 revenue grew 30.2% YoY to ₹2,773 cr, helped by new capacity and the Indore acquisition. Backing out Q1 (₹1,304 cr revenue, ₹157 cr PAT) gives a derived Q2 of about ₹1,469 cr revenue (+33% YoY) and ₹219 cr PAT (14.9% margin), so growth sped up from +26.6% in Q1. H1 PAT rose a slower 18.6% because finance costs jumped 77%, staff costs rose 23%, EBITDA margin eased to 23.4% from 25.0%, and the prior-year half had ₹35.6 cr of one-off gains; stripping those, underlying margins are roughly flat. On valuation (EV/EBITDA used as the main yardstick for this capital-heavy hospital model, P/E as a cross-check), the stock trades at 36.2x EV/EBITDA and 61x trailing P/E. That is above the 28–40x healthcare P/E band and in the top quartile of the broad market (P77–P80), so it is expensive. The 39x forward P/E and rising sell-side estimates (+6% over 90 days) show strong growth is already priced in. The biggest risk is that new beds (Noida, Indore, Ghaziabad) ramp up occupancy and revenue per bed more slowly than expected while staff and interest costs keep rising, which would squeeze margins at a valuation with little room for disappointment.

fundamental.thesis: Pfizer Ltd is the Indian listed arm of Pfizer Inc., selling branded medicines in India, so it has little exposure to the US patented-drug tariff. It has net cash of ₹3,167 cr, a 47% ROCE and no subsidiaries. Revenue growth has held steady rather than accelerated. H1FY27 revenue rose 10.8% YoY to ₹1,380 cr. Q2FY27 revenue, derived as H1 minus Q1, was about ₹727 cr, roughly +13% YoY, after +8.3% in Q1. Reported H1 PAT jumped 35.9% to ₹518 cr, but that includes a one-time ₹132 cr payment for discontinuing Minipress XL. Stripping it out, underlying PAT grew only about 10%, and EBITDA margin has been choppy in the 38–46% range. On a trailing P/E yardstick (the right one for a branded-formulations business, with EV/EBITDA as a cross-check), the stock trades at 28.7x, at the low end of the 28–40x pharma band. It is also below the broad-market median (P39) on P/E and EV/EBITDA of 19.4x, and sits near its 52-week low (9.5% of range), so I grade it fair with a reasonable entry point rather than cheap. The trailing P/E is flattered by the exceptional gain, so the underlying multiple is about 30x. The biggest risk is the earnings path: cash from operations fell 40% in H1 (CFO/PAT 0.69x), sell-side next-year EPS estimates have been cut 4.3% over 90 days, and the parent's portfolio rationalisation could keep shrinking the product basket.

Vijaya Diagnostic is a Hyderabad-headquartered, consumer-facing (92% B2C) pathology and radiology chain with 168 centres across 27 cities, and is expanding into Bengaluru, West Bengal and now the North-East through the Arya Wellness acquisition. Growth is speeding up: H1FY27 revenue was about ₹486 cr (+24.8% YoY) and PAT about ₹113 cr (+37.5%). By subtraction, Q2FY27 revenue is about ₹255 cr (roughly +26% YoY, up from +22.8% in Q1) and PAT about ₹60 cr, a 23.5% margin. Half-yearly revenue growth has risen from +14.9% to +24.8% over the trend window, EBITDA margin has widened from 42.4% to 43.4%, and earnings are well backed by cash (FY26 CFO/PAT 1.56x). The yardstick is EV/EBITDA, since this is a capital-intensive equipment and centre-rollout business: at 41.9x it is about 80% above the market median (P83), and trailing P/E of 82.8x is far above the 28–40x healthcare range (forward 54.7x, P94), so the stock is expensive even after allowing for its growth. The price sits at about 90% of its 52-week range, so the valuation already assumes the expansion keeps working, which leaves little room for any slowdown in new-city ramp-ups.

fundamental.thesis: Wockhardt is an Indian specialty pharma company that has pivoted away from US generics (exited July 2025) toward a proprietary novel antibiotic pipeline anchored by Zaynich (FDA-approved May 2026) and India branded formulations, with 28 subsidiaries across multiple geographies and ₹32,323 cr market cap. Trailing P/E of 152.43× sits at P98 vs 499 market peers (333% premium to broad-market median 35.2×) and far exceeds the pharma sector median of 28–40×; EV/EBITDA of 52.4× (P90 vs peers) paired with P/B of 6.53× against a meagre 4.0% ROE signals the market is pricing in significant Zaynich pipeline success — graded expensive using EV/EBITDA as primary yardstick per the sector card for capital-intensive specialty pharma. The biggest risk is that extraordinary debt/equity of 42.28 with ₹52 cr in quarterly finance costs leaves minimal margin of safety — any delay in Zaynich commercialization or continued mixed subsidiary performance (18 of 28 subsidiaries unreviewed; 5 audited reporting a net ₹2 cr loss on ₹777 cr revenue) could strain free cash flow and force dilutive capital raises.

fundamental.thesis: IRCTC is the government-backed monopoly on Indian Railways' internet ticketing, catering, tourism, and packaged drinking water (Railneer), benefiting from structural exclusivity but exposed to policy risk and PSU governance constraints. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue accelerated to +18.1% YoY (₹1,370 cr), driven by a 420% surge in Tourism (₹768 cr) and 34% Catering growth (₹732 cr), but the highest-margin segment — Internet Ticketing (80% PBIT margin) — grew only 0.6% YoY, a saturation signal in the core earnings engine; annual PAT growth decelerated sharply from +17.5% (FY25) to +6.0% (FY26) alongside EBITDA margin contraction from 39.1% to 37.3%, confirming that volume-driven revenue is not translating to earnings quality. At 30.1× trailing P/E (P41 vs 473 broad-market peers, -14% discount to median 35.2×, and only 10.2% above its 52-week low), headline valuation looks fair-to-cheap on P/E and at the median on EV/EBITDA (23.4×), but the forward P/E of 23× being priced in is contradicted by 90-day sell-side EPS estimate cuts of -14%, suggesting the market has not fully absorbed the margin deterioration — graded 'fair' with downside skew. The primary risk is a convergence of core ticketing saturation, material GST litigation (₹397+ cr debited in FY26 alone, plus a ₹50 cr anti-profiteering case pending at GSTAT since 2022), and sustained downward EPS revisions that carry a pre-derating pattern in a RISK_OFF macro regime.

fundamental.thesis: ITC Hotels is a leading Indian luxury and upscale hotel chain, demerged from ITC, and since May 2026 has a new branded-residences arm after acquiring Kerala Luxury Resorts (Zuri) and GHK Hospitality. Part of that speed-up is bought rather than organic: the core hotels segment grew 13.8%, the new residences segment added ₹109 cr, and operating cash flow is solid at 1.42x PAT. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for this capital-heavy business, 20.8x sits about 11% below the peer median of 23.3x, P/B of 2.75x is at P30 and trailing P/E of 37x (forward 26x) is near the median, so we grade it fair with mild cheapness, and the price sits at 15% of its 52-week range. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for this capital-intensive business, valuation is fair: the listed 27.8x (P61, against a 23.3x broad-market median) and 46.9x trailing P/E appear to rest on FY26 earnings, and on my trailing-12-month estimates they fall to about 23x and 39x, offset by a 7.1x P/B on 16.2% ROE, a price at 85% of the 52-week range and only 5.6% upside to the mean analyst target. The biggest risk is that the margin jump proves temporary, because sugar's 42% growth supplied roughly half of H1 revenue growth and management gave no guidance; balance-sheet risk looks low, as the Rs 1,229 cr net cash and 2.19x CFO/PAT suggest the 10.46 debt/equity flag is a percentage (about 0.10x), although H1 cash conversion also ran high last year (2.84x) before falling to 1.28x for full-year FY26.

LG Electronics India is a recently listed maker of home appliances and TVs. Appliances are 88% of H1 revenue at a thin 9.4% segment margin, while home entertainment is 12% at a much richer 38.9% margin; the company carries ₹4,569 cr of net cash. Revenue growth has accelerated sharply over the last four periods, from -6.4% in Q3FY26 to +8.1%, then +15.5% in Q1FY27, and H1FY27 revenue is ₹14,613 cr (+17.4% YoY) with PAT of ₹1,142 cr (+26.5%). Taking H1 minus Q1 gives a Q2FY27 estimate of about ₹7,380 cr revenue (roughly +19% YoY) and ₹489 cr PAT, a 6.6% margin that is below Q1's 9.0%, though part of that dip is likely seasonal. Part of the acceleration is also easy comparisons against a weak FY26, when PAT fell 23.5% for the year. Using the sector card's yardstick (consumer discretionary names carry 60–100x P/E), the trailing P/E of 64.8x, forward P/E of 41.2x and EV/EBITDA of 42.5x put the stock at the low end of its group's norms, so I grade it fair. Against the broad market, however, it sits at P81–P92 on every multiple, and the sell-side mean target implies only about 7% upside. The biggest risks are a guidance or demand reset, which typically knocks 25–40% off names at these multiples, and the ₹1,163 cr H1 capex for an unproven automotive electronics business while inventory has risen to ₹3,404 cr.

fundamental.thesis: Meesho is a value-focused Indian e-commerce marketplace with 284 million annual transacting users, and its Q2 FY27 contribution margin was 6.0% of net merchandise value (NMV). Revenue grew 34.0% YoY to Rs 4,120 cr in Q2, slowing from +48.0% in Q1 despite the trend table's 'accelerating' label, while NMV grew a slower 23% (33% on management's festive-aligned basis), orders grew 17%, and the net loss narrowed about 68% YoY to Rs 132 cr at a -3.2% margin, though that margin is roughly flat against the implied Q1 level of about -3.6%. The biggest risk is that the cheapness reflects a structural decline in linear-TV advertising, with earnings increasingly tied to lumpy, cricket-calendar revenue.

The table's 'accelerating' signal is unreliable because the older FY26 rows (₹171–670 cr) are clearly on a different basis. Because this is a capital-intensive manufacturer, I graded it mainly on EV/EBITDA: 15.7x is at P28 versus the broad market and below its median of 23.3x, and P/E of 35x trailing and 26x forward sits near the median. However, P/B of 2.8x against an ROE of only 8% is not cheap, so overall it is fair. The biggest risk is that the profit surge rests on one segment (yarn) while towels deteriorate (revenue -11%, EBIT -47%), just as the company commits to a ₹4,650 cr expansion worth about a third of its market cap.

fundamental.thesis: Vishal Mega Mart is a value-format hypermarket chain for middle- and lower-income shoppers, mainly in Tier-2/3 India. It has 819 stores as of Q1 FY27, up from 742 a year earlier, and same-store sales growth has held steady at 10-11%. EBITDA margin slipped from 14.75% to 14.23% YoY, and PAT growing slower than revenue points to cost pressure. Cash conversion is strong: CFO/PAT is 2.2x, FCF is ₹673 cr and net debt is a minimal ₹137 cr. On valuation I graded on EV/EBITDA and P/E against the sector card's 60-100x norm for premium consumer names. A trailing P/E of 65.9x (44.2x forward) and EV/EBITDA of 29.1x put it at the low end of that band, so fair. It is still not cheap for mid-teens growth: it sits at P81 on P/E in a broad-market peer set, because there are no tight retail peers in the universe. The biggest risk is that growth keeps slowing while the stock carries a premium multiple. Analysts are trimming EPS estimates (FY next -2% over 90 days) while 18 of 19 still rate it a buy, a pattern that often comes before a de-rating. The extracted H1 figures (₹3,877 cr) also look inconsistent with Q1 alone (₹3,727 cr), so treat the trajectory numbers with caution.

On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick we use for this capital-heavy business, the stock trades at 10.3x, cheaper than about 89% of the broad market, and its trailing P/E of 17.4x sits just below the 18-28x auto-ancillary range. That makes it cheap on paper, but sell-side FY EPS estimates were cut about 10% in the last 30 days, so the cheapness is partly a falling-earnings effect. The biggest risk is that lead-acid margins keep shrinking while the loss-making new-energy unit (Rs 64 cr H1 loss) and Rs 2,320 cr of new LFP capex keep free cash flow negative (Rs -161 cr in H1).

Minda Corporation is a domestic-focused auto component maker (electronics, mechatronics, wiring harnesses, EV systems) that is growing content per vehicle across two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle customers. Much of this jump comes from consolidating Minda-VAST from April 2026, so organic growth is lower and cannot be separated from the data given. Q2 PAT was about ₹143 cr (6.5% margin), and H1 PAT of ₹349 cr includes a one-off ₹106 cr gain from that consolidation; excluding it, H1 PAT is about ₹243 cr (about 6.0% margin), so the underlying margin is roughly flat, EBITDA margin is stuck near 11.6–11.8% against 14.2% in FY25, and the 'expanding PAT margin' signal is distorted by the one-off. The biggest risk is that the market is pricing acquisition-boosted growth as if it were organic, while margins have not expanded and the stock already trades near its highs.

fundamental.thesis: Sona BLW makes auto driveline components with a heavy EV tilt: battery-EV products were 51% of Q2 FY27 automotive revenue, with BEV revenue up 129% YoY, and the net order book of Rs 25,100 cr is roughly 5x trailing revenue. Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,547 cr (+35.0% YoY) and PAT Rs 223 cr (+29.0%), but both slowed from Q1 (+52.4% and +46.8%), so the pre-computed 'accelerating' revenue signal is misleading, and EBITDA margin has fallen from 27.6% in FY26 to 25.2% and then 23.0%, while PAT margin of 14.4% is up from 13.7% in Q1 but below FY26's 15.7%. On trailing P/E and EV/EBITDA the stock is expensive: 72.0x P/E (+104.6% vs the broad-market median, P84, and well above the 18-28x auto benchmark) and 43.5x EV/EBITDA (P85), though the peer set is a broad-market fallback, FY EPS estimates are up about 5% over 90 days, and the snapshot's 45% dividend yield and 7.21 debt/equity look like data errors, so balance-sheet strength is unconfirmed. The biggest risk is that this price needs strong growth to continue, so further margin slippage or slower EV-linked orders could cause a sharp de-rating.

Tenneco Clean Air India makes exhaust after-treatment and clean-air systems for Indian vehicle makers, a domestic-content auto ancillary that benefits from tighter emission norms. In the latest extracted quarter (Q1 FY27) revenue was ₹1,545 cr, up 20.2% YoY and faster than FY26's +10.5%, but PAT of ₹165 cr fell 1.7% YoY and PAT margin slipped to 10.7% from 11.2% in FY26. Q2 FY27 results were filed on 2026-11-04 but have not been extracted; the H1 FY27 PAT of ₹339 cr implies Q2 PAT of about ₹174 cr, with no Q2 revenue figure available. The Q3FY26 revenue row (₹129 cr) is inconsistent with FY26's ₹5,404 cr, so the 'accelerating' trajectory signal rests on partly suspect data. Cash conversion is strong: CFO/PAT was 2.37x in FY26 and 1.38x in H1 FY27. Valuation yardstick: trailing P/E for auto ancillaries, cross-checked with EV/EBITDA. Trailing P/E of 38.2x is above the 18–28x auto band, so I grade it expensive, though forward P/E of 27.7x is at the top of that band and EV/EBITDA of 24.3x is in line with the broad-market median. The biggest long-term risk is that electrification shrinks the market for exhaust systems, a structural loser in the energy-transition theme, while near-term profit is not keeping pace with sales.

fundamental.thesis: ZF CVCS India is a domestic-content auto ancillary supplying braking, transmission (AMT), and safety control systems for commercial vehicles, with a structural EV angle as the sole OEM e-compressor supplier for electric buses — a meaningful ASP story given e-bus kits cost ~₹2.25L vs ~₹45K for standard CV kits (~5× uplift). Q1FY27 revenue grew +9.3% YoY to ₹1,066 cr (a recovery from flat FY25 and near-zero H1 FY26), but PAT fell 14.6% YoY to ₹104 cr (9.8% margin) as EBITDA margin compressed 505 bps from 20.3% to 16.3% — textbook negative operating leverage; the margin trajectory has been consistently contracting from 22.9% (Q2FY26) through 20.0% (Q3FY26) to 16.3% (Q1FY27) and is the dominant concern. The valuation snapshot's trailing P/E of 2.83× is almost certainly corrupted by the June 2026 5:1 bonus split distorting yfinance EPS; using trend-table LTM PAT of ~₹498 cr against ₹29,000 cr market cap implies an estimated trailing P/E of ~58×, well above the 18–28× Auto sector median — graded expensive — and the forward P/E of 38.28× (itself above sector median) confirms earnings are expected to remain well below recent peaks. The key risk is that persistent margin compression and 90-day EPS estimate cuts of 5.8%, combined with a CFO transition in September 2026 and a RISK_OFF macro, leave no near-term catalyst for re-rating toward fundamental value.

fundamental.thesis: AWL Agri Business sells edible oils under the Fortune brand, along with packaged foods and industrial inputs such as oleochemicals, and reaches about 135 million households, but it earns thin margins typical of a commodity processor rather than a premium FMCG company. Revenue growth accelerated from +18% in Q1 to about +26% in Q2 (roughly Rs 22,202 cr, derived as H1 minus Q1), and H1 volume growth of 11% extends the improvement from 2-3% in Q2-Q3 FY26 and 7% in Q1 FY27, but Q2 PAT swung from +48% to about -2% YoY (Rs 239 cr vs Rs 245 cr), partly due to a Bangladesh minimum tax, while PAT margin fell from 1.8% to about 1.1%, so the 'expanding' margin signal in the trend table, which mixes half-year and quarterly periods, looks unreliable. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, the stock looks fair, leaning cheap, at 9.0x (P8) and 20.7x trailing P/E near its 52-week low, because the broad-market peer set and 40-65x FMCG norm are poor comparisons for a 3% EBITDA-margin business, and 2.29x book for an estimated 11% ROE is not a clear bargain; the 54% dividend yield and 10.62 debt/equity look like data errors (debt/equity is probably about 0.11x), and the +55.6% consensus upside looks overstated because the implied price is below the 52-week low. The biggest risk is that growth keeps failing to reach profit, since edible oil volumes grew only 5%, EBITDA of Rs 4,100/MT sits at the low end of the Rs 4,000-4,500 guidance, and small moves in input costs can have an outsized effect on a margin this thin.

DOMS Industries is a branded stationery and art-materials maker (pencils, pens, paper products) with a smaller, fast-growing hygiene segment. It is tagged FMCG here even though yfinance lists it as Industrials. Revenue is still growing, but growth has slowed every period, from +26.4% in Q1FY26 and +24.1% in Q2FY26 to +17.6% in Q2FY27 (₹668 cr). Profit has gone the other way: Q2FY27 PAT fell 37% YoY to ₹38 cr from ₹61 cr, PAT margin dropped from 10.7% to 5.7%, and H1 EBITDA margin was 12.2% against 17.3% for FY26. The pressure comes partly from the low-margin hygiene segment (6.6% operating margin vs 13.5% for stationery) and from heavy capex (about 16% of revenue, which pushed H1 free cash flow to -₹106 cr). Using P/E against the FMCG card's 40–65× norm, the trailing 59.4× sits inside the range but at its top end, so I grade it fair. That multiple is stretched for a company whose earnings are falling, with ROE of about 12% against P/B of 10.6×, while the 52-week position (13% of range) and forward P/E of 40.5× look tempting only if margins recover. The biggest risk is that the margin squeeze persists: sell-side FY EPS estimates have been cut about 13% in 30 days while 12 of 13 ratings stay at buy, a classic pre-derating pattern, and the Company Secretary resigned on results day.

fundamental.thesis: E.I.D. Revenue growth has slowed from +29.3% in Q1 FY26 to +18.3% in Q3 FY26 and +3.4% (Rs 9,018 cr) in Q1 FY27, with the NACL acquisition's boost lapsing from August 2026, while PAT fell 42.5% to Rs 142 cr, EBITDA margin slipped from 10.3% to 8.7%, sugar revenue fell 62% after the refinery closure, and distillery revenue fell 13.5%. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick, with P/B as a cross-check, the stock looks cheap at 5.96x (P2 of the broad market, with no tight peers) and 1.53x book, despite a less clear 29.06x trailing P/E, but consolidated multiples include profit owed to minority holders, some discount looks earned, and the 10.1x forward P/E rests on one analyst whose estimates were cut about 30% in 90 days. The biggest risk is that low price masks weak earnings quality, as FY26 CFO/PAT was only 0.02x, FCF was Rs -64 cr, and the Q2 FY27 results due on 13 Nov could bring further cuts; some extracted figures also look unreliable, including the Rs 61,000 cr refinery investment, the 23.65 debt/equity reading (possibly 23.65%, or about 0.24x) and the +67.6% target upside (about +39% at the implied price near Rs 756).

fundamental.thesis: Gillette India is a P&G-affiliate premium FMCG company with a near-duopoly position in branded men's grooming (razors/blades) and a fast-growing oral care segment, operating debt-free with consistently strong cash conversion (CFO/PAT 0.93× in FY26). Q1FY27 revenue grew +10.8% YoY to ₹783 cr and PAT grew +9.4% YoY to ₹159 cr (PAT margin 20.4%), though growth has decelerated from the Q3FY26 peak of +15.2%; on the positive side, PAT margins have expanded from the Q2FY26 trough of 17.7% to 20.4% now, and the Oral Care segment surged +18.9% YoY, signalling real category momentum. Using the FMCG sector P/E benchmark of 40–65×, the trailing P/E of 35.6× sits below the lower bound — CHEAP on a sector-specific yardstick — though the stock trades at just 3% of its 52-week range (near ₹7,206 low vs ₹10,553 high), a falling-knife flag that demands caution despite the valuation discount. The biggest risk is that advertising costs surging +20.3% YoY, a company secretary resignation in September 2026, and a sustained RISK_OFF macro (FII selling, rising crude) could cap re-rating even if fundamentals hold.

Honasa Consumer (Mamaearth, The Derma Co and other brands) is a digital-first personal-care challenger in FMCG, competing mainly through D2C, quick-commerce and expanding offline retail. H1FY27 revenue grew +31.2% YoY to ₹1,487 cr and PAT more than doubled (+103.2%) to ₹164 cr, with PAT margin expanding to 11.0% and EBITDA margin to 16.7% (+453 bps YoY), an acceleration from about +16% revenue growth in FY26; Q1FY27 volume growth of 30.5% against 1.5% price/mix suggests real demand, although the sector card warns that volume claims above 10% deserve scepticism. Using P/E and EV/EBITDA, the stock is expensive: trailing P/E of 66.3x is above the 40–60x FMCG range, EV/EBITDA is 62.4x (P93 vs the broad market), and the stock sits at 83% of its 52-week range, so the 42.6x forward P/E and rising analyst estimates (+24% FY-EPS revision over 90 days) are already in the price. The biggest risk is earnings quality: H1 operating cash flow covered only 0.57x of PAT and working capital is building up, so any slowdown in growth at this multiple could cause a sharp de-rating. Several extracted figures look inconsistent (Q1FY27 ₹880 cr would imply Q2 below Q1, Q3FY26 ₹60 cr is implausible, and a 9.59 D/E is unlikely for an asset-light business), so they should be checked against the PDF.

fundamental.thesis: LTM Limited is a mid-cap Indian IT services company (~88,000 employees, 740 active clients) with North America at 73.9% of revenue and Financial Services as its largest vertical (~34%); its revenue trajectory has accelerated meaningfully from +7.1% YoY in Q3FY25 to +18.0% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹11,608 cr), with PAT of ₹1,469 cr (+17.1% YoY), though EBITDA margin is on a contracting path (17.8% in Q1FY27 vs 20.4% in FY26) and sequential momentum was near-zero (+0.1% QoQ) — raising the question of how much of the headline +18% reflects base effects rather than structural acceleration. Trailing P/E of 23.65× sits within the IT sector benchmark range of 22–30×, grading FAIR; however, forward P/E of 17.21× falls significantly below the sector lower bound and the EV/EBITDA of 15.15× is at a 35% discount to the broad-market median (23.3×), and with the stock at just 7.4% of its 52-week range (near lows), risk/reward tilts incrementally toward cheap — primary yardstick used is P/E + EV/EBITDA given the IT services capital-light model. The biggest risk is that a 73.9% US revenue concentration faces the active RISK_OFF macro headwind (IT sector macro underweight, rising US yields), while an anomalously high D/E of 9.58× — atypical for an IT peer and possibly inflated by Ind AS 116 leases plus the pending €160M Randstad acquisition — adds balance-sheet uncertainty that is not yet resolved.

C.E. Info Systems (MapmyIndia) is a domestic digital-maps and location-tech platform with a mostly recurring map data and services franchise plus a growing devices arm. It is less exposed than typical IT names to the AI-services and USD/INR themes in the sector card. H1FY27 revenue grew 15.3% YoY to Rs 271.46 cr and PAT 32.1% to Rs 84.99 cr, a sharp acceleration from FY26's +2.3% revenue and -9.2% PAT, but the quality is thin. Almost all the growth came from devices (+161% YoY to Rs 56.17 cr), while core map data and services, 79% of revenue, grew just 0.66%, and implied Q2 revenue (about Rs 131 cr) fell from Q1's Rs 140 cr. On the IT P/E yardstick, trailing P/E of 36.9x sits above the 22-30x IT services band, but forward P/E of 22.5x falls inside it, and the stock is roughly market-median against broad peers (P53 on P/E, P64 on EV/EBITDA) while trading near its 52-week low (10.9% of range), so I grade valuation fair rather than cheap. The biggest risk is that the core recurring business has stalled while sell-side EPS estimates keep being cut (-3.0% FY over 90 days, -4.1% next-FY), with rising capex (10.4% of revenue) and receivables, which points to further de-rating rather than a value entry.
