fundamental.thesis: Netweb Technologies builds high-performance computing systems, AI servers and private-cloud hardware in India, so it is a hardware and infrastructure maker rather than a labour-based IT services firm; the sector card's warning that AI deflates services revenue fits it poorly, and AI capex demand is more likely a tailwind. Growth is clearly very strong but hard to measure precisely. Q1 FY27 revenue was about ₹714 cr (+174.5% YoY) with PAT of ₹85 cr (+196.5%), and yfinance shows Q2 FY27 at about ₹1,091 cr revenue and ₹137 cr PAT. However, the extracted H1 FY27 figures (₹2,143 cr revenue, 19.7% PAT margin) do not reconcile with these quarters and come from an OCR-corrupted filing, so the exact Q2 growth rate and margin step-up are unverified; EBITDA margin also eased from 14.9% to 12.2–13.0% across FY26. Valuation is expensive on any yardstick: trailing P/E is 108.7x against an IT median of 22–30x, forward P/E is 60.7x and EV/EBITDA is 79.2x (I used EV/EBITDA as the primary measure for a hardware business), the stock ranks around P94–P96 against the broad market, and it sits at 74% of its 52-week range. Rising sell-side estimates (FY EPS +11.8% over 90 days) support momentum but leave little room for any slip in lumpy, order-driven revenue.

fundamental.thesis: Sagility is a mid-cap healthcare outsourcing company. About 90% of revenue comes from US health insurers (payers) and about 10% from hospitals and other providers. It is tagged IT here, but its demand comes from US healthcare operations, not tech spending. In Q2FY27 revenue was ₹2,032 cr, up 22.5% YoY, and PAT was ₹284 cr, up 13.3%. Growth has slowed from +35.7% (Q3FY26) to +29.1% (FY26) to +25.0% (H1) to +22.5%, and constant-currency growth is only about 12%, so roughly half the headline growth comes from the weak rupee. Reported PAT margin fell to 14.0% from 15.1% a year ago, and adjusted PAT grew only 8.1% even though adjusted EBITDA margin reached a six-quarter high of 26.3%. On valuation, using P/E and EV/EBITDA, the trailing P/E of 21.5x is below the IT sector's 22–30x range and sits at about the 24th percentile of the broad market (there are no close peers in the universe). EV/EBITDA is 11.4x, forward P/E is 15.4x, and cash conversion is strong (CFO/PAT 1.27x), so the stock looks cheap. The biggest risk is client concentration: the top 3 clients are 60% of revenue and the top 10 are 84%, and voluntary attrition is high at 25.7%. Losing or repricing a single large client could hurt badly. The yfinance dividend yield (44%) and debt/equity (11.5) figures look like unit errors, so I ignored them.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Elxsi is a Tata Group engineering R&D services company specialising in embedded systems design for automotive, media & entertainment, and healthcare verticals — a niche deep-tech services player distinct from commodity IT outsourcers, with a strong domestic and global client base in high-complexity design programmes. Revenue growth has inflected sharply from a -3.9% trough in Q2FY26 to +14.7% YoY in H1FY27 (₹2,077 cr), with PAT rising +13.9% to ₹341 cr and PAT margin holding steady at 16.4%; the System Integration segment contributed 28.9% YoY growth, signalling service diversification — however, EBITDA margin has contracted ~290 bps from its peak of 28.1% (Q3FY26) to 25.2% (H1FY27), driven by New Labour Code wage provisions and rising employee benefits costs. Trailing P/E of 40.78× is above the IT sector benchmark upper bound of 30× (expensive on that metric alone), but the forward P/E collapses to 26.22× — within the 22–30× sector range, confirming earnings recovery is priced in — and peer-rank analysis places TATAELXSI at P60 on both trailing and forward P/E (fairly valued per the ≥P75 expensive threshold); at 6.7% of its 52-week range the stock appears sentiment-oversold relative to an improving earnings trajectory, consistent with the FY26 exceptional charge now cycling out of the base. The primary risk is sustained EBITDA margin compression from structural wage inflation and New Labour Code costs, amplified by a persistent negative EPS revision trend (-0.9% over 90 days, -1.2% next-FY) that historically flags further analyst downgrades ahead, and a long-run AI-driven structural threat to engineering services demand that the sector card explicitly flags as unproven in revenue terms.

fundamental.thesis: ACME Solar is a mid-sized renewable power producer (IPP) with 2,990 MW running and about 5,080 MW under construction, and its 25-year power purchase agreements (PPAs) are mostly with central-government buyers like NTPC. Such a company grows through new capacity and the spread between its returns and its cost of debt, and the new BESS (battery storage) and FDRE (round-the-clock renewable) projects are its growth engine. H1 FY27 revenue rose 78.2% YoY to ₹1,745 cr and PAT rose 105% to ₹504 cr. YoY growth has sped up from +59% (FY26) to +63% (Q1) to +78% (H1), and PAT margin rose from 19.9% to 24.7% to 28.9%. Within H1, the September quarter works out to roughly ₹791 cr revenue (below Q1, which fits the monsoon dip in solar output) but higher PAT of about ₹269 cr. Operating capacity barely moved in Q1 (+3.5% YoY), so near-term growth now depends on commissioning, which has started: 66.68 MW of solar plus BESS units went live in early November, and a 400 MW FDRE PPA was signed with NTPC. Valuation is fair: I graded it on EV/EBITDA, the card's yardstick for capital-heavy businesses. At 15.2x it is about 35% below the market median (P26), and the forward P/E of 13.7x is far below the trailing 40.7x, which suggests earnings growth is expected. But P/B of 4.0x against a 10.4% ROE is not cheap, and the stock sits at 80% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is the balance sheet: debt/equity is about 3.9x, interest coverage is only 2.47x, finance costs take about 40% of EBITDA, and H1 free cash flow was -₹5,263 cr on ₹6,329 cr of capex. Grid connection delays (substations delivered on time only 60% of the time, about 6 months late on average) or higher interest rates could hold back the earnings ramp.

fundamental.thesis: RailTel is a state-owned railway telecom and IT-infrastructure company; its legacy telecom services business, which leases the railway fibre network, is now outgrown by lower-margin government project work, so the mobile-telecom sector card (ARPU, oligopoly) does not really apply. For H1 FY27, revenue grew 20.3% YoY to ₹2,039 cr from ₹1,695 cr, but PAT fell 5.5% to ₹134 cr and PAT margin compressed from 8.2% to 6.6%, continuing a slide from 8.9% in Q1 FY26 and 7.8% in 9M FY26. Revenue growth has also cooled from +33% to about +20%, and H1 PBT included ₹39 cr of exceptional items (vs ₹13 cr a year ago), so underlying profit quality is weaker than the headline. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA plus peer rank, not the card's 9-12x mobile-telecom band: 15.3x EV/EBITDA (P27 vs a broad-market median of 23.3x) and 32.6x trailing P/E (P46, near the median) grade it fair, and the forward P/E of 21.6x assumes an earnings recovery that the falling sell-side estimates (-3% over 90 days, 2 of 2 analysts at sell) do not yet support. The biggest risk is cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was -₹42 cr and free cash flow -₹202 cr, so growth is being bought with working capital and capex rather than producing cash.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Communications sells global data connectivity and digital platform services to businesses, with no consumer mobile operation, so the sector card's mobile-tariff and ARPU logic does not apply and EV/EBITDA is the yardstick used here. Revenue growth has picked up from +6.5-6.7% through FY26 to +10.1% YoY in H1FY27 (Rs 13,271 cr). That works out to about Rs 6,688 cr for Q2, up about 9.6%, with the Data segment at +11.2% and Digital platforms at +18.6%. Q2 PAT was about Rs 335 cr (5.0% margin) against Rs 130 cr in Q1, but reported PAT swings widely because of Rs 143 cr of H1 exceptional items, so the steady 19-21% EBITDA margin (21.3% in Q2) is the better quality signal. At 13.7x EV/EBITDA the stock is cheap against the broad market (P22) but slightly above the 9-12x telecom range, and its trailing P/E of 53x sits inside the 35-60x sector band. Together with a forward P/E of 23.9x and a price at 85% of its 52-week range, that grades as fair. The biggest risks are the Rs 7,514 cr DoT AGR demand, about 14% of market cap, with an unread litigation update filed on 2026-10-21, and high leverage, while full-year EPS estimates have been cut 5.4% over 90 days even though most analysts still rate it a buy.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) is a small enterprise and wireline telecom player, not part of the Jio/Airtel mobile oligopoly, and it carries a negative net worth of about ₹-19,983 cr built up from years of losses. Revenue has turned around: H1 FY27 grew 7.2% YoY to ₹611 cr after falling 11-15% in earlier periods. Losses are also narrowing, from ₹-646 cr in H1 FY26 to ₹-131 cr in H1 FY26's equivalent this year, and from ₹-72 cr in Q1 to ₹-59 cr in Q2 FY27 (Q2 PAT margin about -19%). On valuation, EV/EBITDA is the right yardstick here, and at 47x it sits far above the 9-12x telecom norm and at P87 against the broad market, so the stock is expensive. The quoted 187x trailing P/E is not meaningful for a company that is losing money. The biggest risk is the balance sheet: debt-service coverage of just 0.10x and interest coverage of 1.09x leave the company dependent on Tata Group support to refinance its debt, which matters more than the recent improvement in operations.

fundamental.thesis: Reliance is a conglomerate with four main businesses: oil refining and chemicals (O2C), Jio telecom (now listed separately as JPL), retail (RRVL) and new energy. Per the sector card it should be valued business by business (sum of the parts), not as a pure oil company. In Q2FY27 gross revenue was a record ₹362,268 cr, up 27.8% YoY, and PAT was ₹29,550 cr, up 33.8% YoY. Revenue growth has picked up from about -8.5% in FY26 to +24.5% in Q1 and +27.8% in Q2, and PAT margin improved from 6.8% in Q1 to 8.2%. However, much of this growth came from O2C, whose EBITDA rose 67.9% because fuel margins spiked on Middle East supply disruption. Retail PAT fell 24.3% and JioStar PAT fell 13.2%, and only Jio is growing steadily (revenue +11.4%, monthly ARPU ₹218.8). We have no sum-of-the-parts data, so as a fallback we used EV/EBITDA of 12.2x and trailing P/E of 21.7x. These look expensive next to the PSU energy peers (median 9.2x P/E, 6.1x EV/EBITDA), but those peers are policy-priced single businesses and not a fair yardstick for a conglomerate. With forward P/E at 18.0x, earnings estimates raised 15-21% over the last 30 days and the price near its 52-week low, we grade valuation fair, not expensive. The biggest risk is that record O2C margins are a temporary geopolitical windfall while retail and media are shrinking, at a time when ROE is only 9.1% and finance costs are up 24.2%.

fundamental.thesis: ICICI Bank is India's second-largest private-sector bank, with a large retail and business-banking franchise and subsidiaries in life and general insurance. In Q2FY27, consolidated revenue rose 15.8% YoY to ₹88,161cr, up from +6.9% growth in Q1. PAT rose 21.5% YoY to ₹17,389cr, up from +12.6%, but PAT margin slipped from 20.4% to 19.7%. Following the sector card, I value lenders on price-to-book against ROE: P/B of 2.48x with a 16.4% ROE is fair for a top-quality bank, even though it ranks P93 (expensive) on P/B among its 15 bank peers, and the stock sits at 22% of its 52-week range, which makes for a reasonable entry point. The biggest risk is that management expects two more 25bp repo hikes and says NIM will only bottom after Q3, so margins could compress further before they recover.

State Bank of India is the country's largest lender, with a ₹78.88 trillion balance sheet, and its asset quality is the best in more than 20 years: gross NPA is 1.39%, net NPA 0.36% and provision coverage 74.43%. In Q2FY27 revenue was ₹151,084 cr (+8.2% YoY, a slight pickup from +7.8% in Q1) and reported PAT was ₹23,038 cr (+14.3% YoY). That profit includes a ₹7,288 cr one-time gain from the SBI Funds stake sale, against a ₹4,593 cr Yes Bank gain a year earlier, so underlying profit growth is close to flat. Core earnings are also being squeezed: whole-bank NIM slipped to 2.94% (from 3.03% in Q4FY26), fee income fell 4.9% YoY and the cost-to-income ratio rose to 49.82%. On the lender yardstick named in the sector card (P/B vs ROE), the stock trades at 1.53x book for a 15.5% TTM ROE, which is right at the cheap/fair boundary. It sits mid-pack against peers (P/B P57, trailing P/E 10.8x at P36) and at 45% of its 52-week range, so overall it is fairly valued rather than a clear bargain. The main risk is that loans (+17.8%) are growing much faster than deposits (+12.3%) while CASA falls (39.46% to 38.32%). That points to higher funding costs and further margin pressure, and slippages of 0.50% hint that bad loans may start creeping up after a strong run.

fundamental.thesis: ITC is a conglomerate whose profits still come mainly from cigarettes, with FMCG, paper, agri and hotels-adjacent businesses around it; the sector card notes it trades on its own conglomerate multiple backed by dividends, so it should not be read as a pure FMCG name. Cigarette net revenue fell -21% and segment results fell -27%, which drove consolidated EBITDA down -16%; non-cigarette businesses offset part of this, with EBITDA up +22%, FMCG Others revenue up +19% (a 14-quarter high) with margins up 50 bps, and paper PBIT up +48%. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA plus peer rank because ITC is a conglomerate: at 12.1x EV/EBITDA and 16.9x trailing P/E it is the cheapest of 13 FMCG peers on every multiple (around 60-67% below the sector median of 51.5x P/E), near its 52-week low, and cash conversion has improved (CFO/PAT 0.96x vs 0.59x a year ago), so it is cheap. The cheapness looks like a tax-driven structural de-rating rather than a mispricing, and analysts keep cutting earnings estimates (FY EPS -4.8% over 90 days), so the multiple may stay low until cigarette volumes stabilise.

Using P/E cross-checked with EV/EBITDA, the stock looks cheap at 16.9x trailing earnings, below the 18-30x OEM range and 37.7% under the peer median of 27.1x, with EV/EBITDA of 12.2x against a peer median of 18.3x, although P/B is slightly above median and some discount may reflect commuter-bike exposure; I ignored the 307% dividend yield and 3.57 debt/equity as likely unit errors. The biggest risk is that growth and margins disappoint together, as management expects H2 industry growth of only mid to high single digits (low single digits for petrol models) amid commodity inflation, and the standalone EBITDA margin of 13.3% is still below the 14-16% target corridor.

fundamental.thesis: Shriram Finance is one of India's largest retail NBFCs, mainly lending against commercial vehicles, and it now has a 20% strategic shareholder in MUFG Bank, which put in ₹39,618 cr of fresh equity. In Q2 FY27 (H1 minus Q1 from the filings), revenue was about ₹13,774 cr, up 15.6% YoY, and PAT was ₹3,684 cr, up 59.1% YoY. Revenue growth has eased from +19.1% to about +16% while PAT margin widened from 19.0% to 26.7%, partly because the MUFG equity lowers borrowing needs, so the PAT jump overstates the gain in underlying loan economics (loan growth is ~15%). Valuation is graded on P/B plus ROE, the lender yardstick: P/B of 2.56x against ROE of 16.4% (diluted by the new capital) is fair rather than cheap, with P/B at P33 and trailing P/E of 16.8x at P44 among credit-services peers, and forward P/E of 12.9x plus +3.7% upward EPS revisions support the earnings path. The main watch-point is asset quality: gross NPA has crept up from 4.54% to 4.65% standalone and impairment charges rose 27.5% against roughly 15% loan growth, even though net NPA and provision coverage are improving.

fundamental.thesis: Avenue Supermarts (DMART) is India's dominant value-format grocery retailer (~500 stores, FY26) built on an everyday-low-price model with best-in-class inventory turnover (4.93× for H1FY27), giving it durable structural advantages in organised grocery. H1FY27 revenue grew +16.4% YoY to ₹38,439 cr (steady within a consistent +13–16% band over six periods), but PAT grew only +10.0% to ₹1,603 cr as PAT margin contracted to 4.17% from 4.4% — finance costs surged 84% to fund aggressive expansion, the Avenue E-commerce subsidiary dragged ₹166.62 cr in losses, and CFO/PAT collapsed from 0.96× (H1FY26) to 0.34× (H1FY27), signalling a meaningful deterioration in earnings quality. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary valuation yardstick (capital-intensive retail with PAT margins distorted by lease and e-commerce costs), DMART trades at 52.4× EV/EBITDA — P100 (most expensive) among 13 Consumer Discr. peers and +51% above the sector median — while trailing P/E of 89.1× is also P100 and +73% above sector median; sell-side EPS estimates have been revised down -3.1% over 90 days, a textbook pre-derating signal. The biggest risk is that the quick-commerce threat from Blinkit erodes SSSG momentum just as e-commerce losses widen and leverage builds, triggering the 25–40% multiple reset the sector card explicitly flags for any guidance disappointment at these premium valuations.

Ambuja Cements, the Adani group's cement platform with about 109 MTPA of capacity, is one half of a consolidating duopoly with UltraTech and is building toward 155 MTPA by FY30 with roughly ₹14,500 cr of self-funded capex. The trend is clearly getting worse: H1 FY27 revenue fell 3.8% YoY to ₹18,640 cr (Q1 was -7.6%), and Q2 PAT was only ₹236 cr, a 2.6% margin, down from 6.1% in Q1 and about 14% in FY26. Q2 EBITDA/tonne dropped to ₹770, below the ₹900–1,100 healthy band and down from ₹887 in FY26, as fuel costs rose to ₹1.87 per 1,000 kcal and total volumes stayed flat. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for capital-intensive cement, the stock trades at 18.5×, about in line with the sector median of 17.9× (P53), so it grades fair. The P20 trailing P/E looks cheap only because the peer set includes premium paint names, and the forward P/E of 26.9× sitting above the trailing 22× confirms that earnings are expected to fall. The biggest risk is that elevated imported-fuel prices (spot about ₹2.80/kcal) and rising crude push costs past the ₹4,250/t target before the Penna/Sanghi assets (running at about 50% utilisation) and the new capacity ramp up, which would justify the ongoing 49–68% cuts to FY-EPS estimates.

fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Holdings is a near debt-free holding company whose value comes from its stakes in Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv. Its own income is mostly dividends and interest, so it is better judged on portfolio value per share (NAV) than on revenue. H1FY27 revenue fell 20.1% YoY to ₹576 cr because Bajaj Auto paid less in dividends after its buyback. Reported PAT fell 6.7% to ₹4,845 cr, but the prior year included a one-off ₹1,522 cr gain on selling Bajaj Finserv shares; without that gain, underlying PAT grew about 37%, and the share of associate profits rose 32% to ₹4,626 cr (Bajaj Auto Q2 PAT +62%, Bajaj Finserv +23%). Using the holding-company NAV-discount yardstick from the sector card, the stock trades at roughly a 50% discount to its ₹21,578 per-share NAV, inside the normal 40–60% band, so valuation is fair rather than cheap. The 11.4x trailing P/E (P33 vs Financials peers) and 1.5x P/B with 12.6% ROE point the same way, while the EV/EBITDA (127.6x) and dividend yield (157%) figures are not meaningful for this structure or are data errors and were ignored. The main risk is that the stock simply tracks two Bajaj group companies and the NAV discount may never narrow, with the pending RBI Core Investment Company re-classification adding regulatory uncertainty.

fundamental.thesis: ICICIPRULI (now ICICI Life Insurance) is one of India's largest private life insurers, with ₹3.29 lakh cr of assets under management, a 229.9% solvency ratio and a 99.3% claim-settlement ratio. New business has picked up after a flat FY26: in H1FY27, annualised premium equivalent (APE) grew +15.1% YoY to ₹4,935 cr (FY26 was only +2.2%), retail APE recovered from -0.1% to +9.9%, VNB grew +22.3% to ₹1,283 cr, and VNB margin widened to 26.0% from 24.7% in FY26. Gross premium grew +15.3% to ₹24,505 cr and PAT +26.5% to ₹760 cr, but PAT is not the right yardstick for a life insurer. On the life-insurer yardstick, price to embedded value (P/EV), the stock trades at about 1.24x (₹70,497 cr market cap vs ₹56,669 cr EV, which grew +12.2% YoY; FY26 return on EV was 11.9%), which looks cheap. Peer ranks agree: P25 on P/B and forward P/E, at a 22–25% discount to the peer median. The biggest risk is growth fading: management has guided that protection growth will cool from the 40–50% pace of the last four quarters, and Prudential's pending reclassification from promoter to investor could mean an overhang of stake sales, while the market is in a RISK_OFF regime.

Siemens is one of India's leading electrical, automation and mobility equipment makers, with a net cash position of about ₹8,113 cr. That positions it squarely in the transmission, data-centre and rail capex cycle. In Q2FY27 revenue rose 17.0% YoY to ₹5,734 cr, accelerating from +14.6% and +14.8% in the prior two periods, and new orders jumped 37.8% to ₹6,228 cr, with the order backlog up 12% to ₹47,034 cr (roughly 2x annualised revenue). However, PAT grew only 3.9% to ₹504 cr, an 8.8% margin, and management cites commodity and foreign-exchange pressure on material costs, with operating margin falling from 11.4% to 9.5%; Q1's 45.5% PAT margin is distorted by the one-off gain on the motors-business sale and should be ignored. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for this order-book business, 52.8x is about 55% above the 34x peer median (around the 76th percentile), and trailing P/E of 76.5x sits at the top of even the 50–80x electricals band. With full-year EPS estimates cut 4.5% over 90 days, the stock looks expensive, and the biggest risk is that orders keep growing but margins don't, leaving the premium multiple to de-rate.

fundamental.thesis: Crompton is one of India's largest fan, pump and small-appliance makers. It leads the market in ceiling fans, reaches about 2.5 lakh retailers, and gained share across most categories between FY23 and FY26 (water heaters +200 bps, residential pumps +180 bps). In Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to ₹2,235 cr and PAT rose about 15% to ₹143 cr (PAT margin 6.4%), up from +7.3% revenue growth in Q3 FY26. But EBITDA margin slipped from about 11% to about 10%, because the company passed on only about 80% of cost inflation despite 10–15% price hikes, and it lost roughly ₹200 cr of primary sales to supply disruption. fundamental.thesis: Indiamart runs a large Indian B2B online marketplace, with 8.9 million supplier storefronts and 217 thousand paying suppliers, and earns mainly from advance-paid supplier subscriptions, which makes it a platform rather than a typical consumer company. Comparing like quarters (the pre-computed trend signals mix quarterly and full-year figures), Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9.7% YoY to Rs 429 cr, slowing from +12% a year earlier, while PAT rose about 10% to Rs 91 cr, EBITDA margin improved from 33% to 37%, and PAT margin stayed flat near 21%; however, paying suppliers fell 2% and collections grew only 9%, so growth depends on higher revenue per supplier rather than more customers, though cash conversion is strong at 1.48x CFO/PAT. Valuation is fair using a platform yardstick of EV/EBITDA and unit economics: EV/EBITDA of 18.1x and trailing P/E of 27.1x sit below the broad-market medians of 23.3x and 35.2x (no close peers are available), and cash of Rs 3,234 cr is about 25% of market cap, but trailing P/E rests on FY26 PAT of Rs 475 cr, while annualising the latest quarter gives about 35x, and the 20.7x forward P/E assumes a profit recovery that the Rs 91 cr quarter does not yet show. Sundaram Finance is a conservatively run, Chennai-based vehicle-finance NBFC. Its group also includes housing finance, an asset manager and a general-insurance joint venture, and it is known for some of the best asset quality in its peer set. The Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-11-05 show standalone quarterly PAT of ₹475 cr (+21% YoY), H1FY27 consolidated PAT of ₹1,153 cr (+20%), disbursements up 28% YoY in Q2 (H1 +25%) and core lending AUM up 19% to ₹65,992 cr. Gross Stage 3 improved to 1.84% from 2.03% and provision cover rose to 51% from 45%. One caution is that Q2 profit from operations grew only 11%, so part of the profit growth is coming from lower credit costs rather than core earnings; the pre-computed 'margin contracting' signal comes from mixed revenue bases and is not meaningful. On the lender yardstick (P/B against sustainable ROE), P/B of 3.5x against ROE of 16.75% (up from 15.9%) is fair to slightly rich: the stock is at P67 on P/B and P100 on forward P/E within its credit-services peer group, though the cheapest peers are the state-owned power lenders PFC and REC, a lower-quality comparison set. The biggest near-term risk is the chairman's resignation announced alongside results, alongside a capital adequacy ratio that slipped to 18.5% from 19.3% and a ₹66 cr Motor TP claims provision at Royal Sundaram after the Supreme Court judgment.

fundamental.thesis: PFC is India's largest government-owned infrastructure finance NBFC, the apex lender to the power sector (generation, transmission, distribution) and parent of REC Limited, with a combined consolidated AUM of ~₹10L+ cr — a proposed merger (PFC absorbs REC at 88:100, effective April 2027) would make it one of Asia's largest infrastructure lenders. Q1FY27 revenue was essentially flat at −0.04% YoY (₹28,527 cr) with PAT barely moving at +0.18% YoY (₹8,998 cr, 31.5% margin), loan book growth of only 7% YoY, and rising forex losses (₹837 cr vs ₹706 cr prior year) — a sharp deceleration from Q4/FY26's 16% PAT growth and a clear single-quarter slowdown, though CFO/PAT of 1.81x confirms earnings quality remains cash-backed. Using P/B + ROE — the correct yardstick per sector card for lenders — PFC at 1.08x P/B with 20.5% ROE is unambiguously cheap (threshold: P/B < 1.5 + ROE > 12% = cheap), and is ranked P0 (cheapest in peer group) on both P/B (1.1x vs sector median 3.0x) and trailing P/E (5.6x vs sector median 20.1x); asset quality is exceptional with GNPA 0.66% and net NPA 0.13%. The primary risk is that forward P/E (6.7x) exceeds trailing P/E (5.6x) — a market signal that earnings are expected to decline — compounded by PFC-REC merger integration complexity and EPS dilution risk from the 88:100 exchange ratio, all set against a RISK_OFF macro regime with sustained FII outflows (−₹41,850 cr 30-day net) that create a structural re-rating headwind for PSU financials.

fundamental.thesis: Alkem Laboratories is India's #3 pharmaceutical company by prescriptions and #1 in trade generics, operating a ~68% domestic branded-generic franchise supplemented by fast-growing international arms (US +20.3%, ROW +26.7% in FY26). FY26 revenue grew +13.5% YoY to ₹14,712 cr with EBITDA expanding +19.6% to ₹3,052 cr (20.4% margin), but PAT growth lagged at only +6.3% (₹2,302 cr, 15.6% margin) due to a revised upward tax rate and ~₹1,350 cr in Q4FY26 exceptional charges (gratuity liability reclassification + real estate impairment); PAT margin has structurally contracted from 19.4% in H1FY26 to 15.6% for FY26, and cash conversion is weak at 0.59× CFO/PAT. At 27.4× trailing P/E — fractionally below the 28-40× sector benchmark and at P31 among 14 pharma peers against a sector median of 36.4× — Alkem is fairly valued with a moderate discount; forward P/E of 23.1× signals earnings growth is priced in, and EV/EBITDA of 20.2× is modestly below the 21.4× peer median, leaving limited re-rating upside without a catalyst. The dominant risk to the thesis is the simultaneous departure of the CEO and CFO (both transitions flagged in FY27 filings), creating a senior management vacuum precisely when the Occlutech MedTech acquisition is pending integration, trade-generic growth is stalling at +4.3% YoY, and the US tariff framework for generics remains under an active one-year Commerce review.

fundamental.thesis: Supreme Industries is India's largest plastics processor, selling plastic pipes (including CPVC), industrial, packaging and consumer products through about 50,000 distributors. Dixon Technologies is India's largest contract electronics maker (EMS). It assembles smartphones, TVs, lighting, IT hardware and telecom gear, and is building camera-module and display capacity under the PLI scheme and the China+1 shift. The filed H1 FY27 figures show revenue of ₹37,938 cr and PAT of ₹1,129 cr, with PAT up 51% YoY. That leaves an implied Q2 of about ₹21,900–22,400 cr revenue and ₹411–466 cr PAT, which is only about a 2% PAT margin against 4.3–4.5% in Q1 FY27. Q1 revenue grew +21% to +25% (the two extracted Q1 rows disagree). The reported +147% H1 revenue growth and the ₹4,959 cr FY26 row do not reconcile with the quarterly figures, so the growth rate cannot be trusted. Margins are being diluted as volume grows faster than profit. Because this is an assembly-heavy, low-margin business, I graded on EV/EBITDA plus trailing P/E. EV/EBITDA is 32.3x, and trailing P/E of 42.9x sits at the top of the 28–45x Industrials range, so I grade it fair-to-full rather than cheap even though the stock is only 22% up its 52-week range. The peer-rank block compares Dixon with IT-services companies (WIPRO, INFY, PERSISTENT), which are not real peers, so I gave its 'P100 expensive' verdict little weight. The forward P/E is above the trailing P/E, and analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 7% over 30 days and 10% over 90 days while ratings stay 22 buy. That pattern often comes before a de-rating. FY26 cash conversion was also weak: cash from operations was only 0.22x PAT and free cash flow was -₹271 cr.

fundamental.thesis: Angel One is one of India's largest retail stockbrokers by active clients, so it earns mainly from broking fees (heavily F&O-linked), interest on client margin funding and distribution. But this follows a weak FY26 (revenue -1.9%, PAT -21.9%), so much of the rebound is a recovery from a low base rather than proven new growth. The Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-10-15 are not yet in the extracted data. For a fee-based broker I graded on P/E cross-checked with P/B against ROE: trailing P/E of 35.8x is above the 18–28x NBFC/capital-markets band and in line with the broad market (P52), while forward P/E of 20.3x prices in a further earnings recovery. In H1 FY27, revenue grew 21.4% YoY to ₹3,566 cr: plumbing rose 18.2% at a 12.9% segment margin and paints & adhesives rose 29.0%, but that segment's margin is only about 3.1%. PAT grew more slowly, up 15.7% to ₹248 cr (6.9% margin), and operating cash flow swung to -₹68 cr from +₹389 cr a year ago because of a large tax outflow, inventory build-up and 29% higher capex. The prior-period rows in the trend table are clearly wrong (for example, Q4FY26 revenue of ₹17,347 cr), so there is no reliable multi-quarter trend to rely on. On the sector card's preferred yardstick, EV/EBITDA is 35.7×, about 5% above the peer median of 34.0× (P59). Trailing P/E is 68.2× against a peer median of 53.8× (P62), and forward P/E is 43.3×, which already prices in earnings growth. That makes the stock fairly valued: there is no clear mispricing, though it sits at 32% of its 52-week range, which is a reasonable but not compelling entry point. The biggest risk is quality of growth. Profit is lagging revenue, cash conversion turned negative, paints is a low-margin segment, and the ₹95 mn goodwill impairment on Seal It (US) shows past acquisitions have not all paid off.

fundamental.thesis: GIC Re is India's dominant state-owned reinsurer. It takes on risk from domestic insurers across fire, motor, health, agriculture and other lines, and AM Best rates it A- (Excellent) with a stable outlook. In H1 FY27, gross written premium grew 11.7% year on year to ₹24,713 cr, faster than the +5.8% to +6.4% of FY26 and H1 FY26. Profit fell the other way: consolidated PAT dropped 12.8% to ₹4,709 cr, PAT margin shrank from 26.8% to 19.1%, and the combined ratio worsened slightly from 106.36% to 106.79%. That means the company loses money on underwriting and relies on ₹5,015 cr of investment income. Q2 alone (about ₹2,966 cr of PAT, implied by H1 minus Q1) was much better than Q1, whose PAT fell 31%. For an insurer I grade value on price-to-book against ROE, not P/E. At 0.62x book, the cheapest in the peer set and near the bottom of its 52-week range, the stock is cheap even for a below-par 9.1% ROE, and the 4.18x solvency ratio gives a large capital buffer. The trailing P/E of 6.8x supports this but is not my yardstick. The ROE gap is the main reason the market keeps this PSU at a discount to book. The biggest risk is that underwriting losses stay above 100% of premium while estimates keep being cut (FY EPS down 10% over 90 days), so earnings would depend on volatile investment gains.

Authum Investment & Infrastructure is a mid-cap NBFC and investment holding company. Its earnings come mainly from gains on its investment portfolio and from buying distressed assets through the insolvency (NCLT) process, so profits swing a lot from quarter to quarter. It does not run a steady lending book. In Q2FY27, revenue rose 12.6% YoY to ₹685 cr, but PAT fell 45.5% YoY to ₹418 cr and PAT margin dropped to 61.0% from 74.6% in Q1. Revenue growth has also slowed, from +21.4% in Q1 to +12.6%. H1FY27 cash flow from operations was negative at -0.49x PAT, which means reported profits are not turning into cash. For a lender or holding company, P/B against ROE is the right yardstick, not P/E. On that basis the stock is fair rather than cheap: P/B is 2.91x for an ROE of 13.1%, well above the 'cheap' bar of P/B under 1.5 with ROE over 12%. The headline trailing P/E of 8.95x, in the bottom 5% of the market, overstates how cheap it is because it rests on large investment gains that may not repeat. The biggest risk is that earnings depend on market-linked investment gains and lumpy distressed-asset deals, and profits are not backed by cash. Leverage is also unclear: the live snapshot shows debt/equity of 24.59, which is unverified and could be a percentage misread.

fundamental.thesis: GPIL is an integrated steel and power producer (iron ore pellets → sponge iron → billets/wire rods with captive power) headquartered in Chhattisgarh, recently allotting industrial land at AURIC Bidkin, Maharashtra, signalling a next-phase capacity push. Revenue has deteriorated from near-flat +0.8% YoY in H1FY26 to -11.4% YoY in Q3FY26 (₹1,166 cr), while PAT margin compressed steadily from 16.3% in Q1FY26 to 12.3% in Q3FY26 — both revenue growth and margins are moving in the wrong direction over four consecutive periods. Assessed on EV/EBITDA of 13.5× (the appropriate yardstick for a capital-intensive steel business; P/E is secondary), GPIL trades at a 42% discount to the broad-market median of 23.3× and sits at P22 of 473 peers — genuinely cheap, but the discount reflects real fundamental headwinds rather than neglected quality; a forward P/E of 10.9× versus trailing 19.5× implies the market is pricing in an earnings recovery that the current revenue trajectory has not yet validated. The primary threat to any recovery thesis is extreme financial leverage (D/E 7.58) paired with sustained sell-side EPS cuts (-19.1% over 90 days from only one covering analyst), which compresses the margin of safety materially if the steel-price downcycle extends into FY27.

Escorts Kubota is one of India's major tractor makers and also sells construction equipment. Agri machinery brings in about 87% of revenue, so it trades more like a farm-equipment and auto-cyclical stock than a capital-goods order-book business. In H1 FY27 revenue rose 21.9% to ₹6,451 cr, but the implied Q2 numbers are weak: revenue of about ₹3,243 cr is up only about 16% YoY, slower than Q1's +28.3%, and PAT of about ₹250 cr is down about 21% YoY, so PAT margin fell to about 7.7% from 12.0% in Q1. Agri EBIT margin fell 340 bps to 9.3% on higher commodity costs and a weaker product mix, operating cash flow turned negative (-₹107 cr) as inventory and receivables built up, and management now expects margins to return to normal only in FY28. I graded valuation on P/E and EV/EBITDA against farm-equipment and auto peers, because the Industrials order-book yardstick does not fit this business. A trailing P/E of 22.6x is mid-range for auto (18-28x) and well below the Industrials band, EV/EBITDA is 16.3x and P/B is 2.5x against a 12% ROE, so it is fair, not cheap. Analysts have cut this year's EPS estimate by 11.6% in 30 days, which explains the discount and the stock sitting near its 52-week low. Some inputs conflict: the dividend yield, the price implied by the 52-week range versus the analyst target, debt/equity of 1.31 against a reported net-cash position, and a Q2 EBITDA margin that works out to an implausible ~2.6%. So I am trusting the reported revenue and PAT more than the derived ratios.

fundamental.thesis: GE Vernova T&D India is India's leading power transmission and distribution equipment maker (transformers, switchgear, grid substations), directly leveraged to the government's ₹9 lakh cr grid build-out through 2032 and a structural T&D order-book upcycle. Jyoti CNC Automation is an Indian maker of CNC machine tools that also owns the Huron group of subsidiaries in France, Germany, Canada, Turkey and China, so its results depend on demand from manufacturing and defence capex. Sales are growing well but profits are shrinking. H1 FY27 revenue rose 21.0% YoY to ₹1,110 cr, and the implied Q2 FY27 (H1 minus Q1) was about ₹602 cr, up roughly 18.5%. Consolidated PAT, however, fell 17.4% to ₹130 cr in H1, and implied Q2 PAT fell about 15% to roughly ₹73 cr. PAT margin dropped from 16.8% to about 12.1% and EBITDA margin from 26.3% to 21.6%, mostly because overseas subsidiaries lost ₹73 cr in H1. Valuation is fair but rich: I used EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-intensive name, and at 31.6× it sits at P67 against the broad market. Trailing P/E of 47.4× is just above the 28–45× Industrials band, and P/B of 8.0× is high for an 18% ROE. The forward P/E of 28.3× and rising estimates (+15% over 90 days) assume a profit recovery the filings do not show yet. The filings give no order-book or order-inflow figures, which are the sector's key metrics, so I cannot check revenue visibility. The biggest open risk is the French judicial investigation of Huron Graffenstaden for alleged dual-use export violations. It sits on top of rising subsidiary losses and negative free cash flow.

fundamental.thesis: IRB Infrastructure is India's largest private toll-road operator and developer. It runs 27 highway projects with about 1.5 million vehicles crossing its plazas each day, a share of about 10% of India's toll revenue, and an asset base of about ₹94,000 cr. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹1,945 cr, up 8.1% YoY, recovering from +0.4% in Q1FY27 and -20.1% for FY26. PAT was ₹260 cr, up 84.4% YoY, for a 13.4% margin, and EBITDA was ₹1,102 cr at a 56.7% margin, up 13%. Two cautions on these numbers: much of the PAT jump comes from InvIT distributions and asset transfers rather than from tolls, and the earlier trend rows look like a mix of standalone and consolidated figures, so the YoY bases are not fully comparable. This is a capital-heavy toll business, so I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, which is 16.2× against a broad-market median of 23.3× (P29). Overall I grade it fair, not cheap. The main risk is debt: net debt is ₹10,283 cr, about 2.3× annualised EBITDA, and earnings depend on InvIT monetisation. Meanwhile analysts have cut their FY EPS estimates by 4.2% (current year) and 6.8% (next year) over the last 30 days, even though all 5 still rate it a buy.

fundamental.thesis: Shyam Metalics is an integrated metals producer (ferro alloys, steel long products, pellets, aluminium foil) with captive power; it is tagged Industrials here but behaves like a Materials business, so this grade relies mainly on EV/EBITDA rather than order-book metrics. Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹5,455 cr, up 23.3% YoY. That is slower than Q3 FY26's +34.6% but in line with FY26's +22.4%. PAT was ₹351 cr (+20.6% YoY, 6.4% margin), though a second extraction shows ₹312 cr (5.7%). Margins are stable to slightly improving versus Q3 FY26's 4.4% PAT margin and 13.6% EBITDA margin; the H1FY26 row (42.8% EBITDA) is clearly a bad extraction and is ignored. Q2 FY27 results came out on 31 Oct, but their figures were not extracted, so the latest quarter is a blind spot. On valuation, EV/EBITDA of 12.3x is in the cheapest fifth of the broad market (P20, 47% below the median), and forward P/E of 15.2x falls within the 12–22x Materials range. Trailing P/E of 25.7x sits above that range, and P/B of 2.5x looks rich for a 9% ROE, so overall the stock grades as fair rather than cheap. Earnings estimates were raised about 23% over the last 30 days, which supports the growth case. The main risks are heavy capex (FY26 free cash flow was -₹614 cr, plus a new ~₹360 cr coal-block plan via the Alom Solar acquisition) and the stock trading near its 52-week high. Several snapshot figures are unreliable: a 47% dividend yield, debt/equity of 8.13 (likely a percentage, not a ratio), and a consensus target implying a price outside the 52-week range.

fundamental.thesis: Schneider Electric Infrastructure is a mid-cap maker of electrical distribution and grid equipment (transformers, switchgear, grid automation), the listed Indian arm of the Schneider group, and it benefits from the power-transmission and data-centre capex cycle. In Q2FY27 revenue grew 19.8% YoY to ₹779 cr, up from +4.8% in Q1FY27, but profit is going the other way: PAT fell 43.3% to ₹30 cr, PAT margin dropped from 8.0% to 3.8% and EBITDA margin from 13.6% to 8.4%. PAT has now fallen YoY for six straight periods, H1FY27 operating cash flow was negative at ₹-29 cr (vs +₹84 cr a year ago), and inventory built up by about ₹115 cr. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card names for capital-intensive industrials, the stock trades at 76.6x, at the top of the 50–80x range for premium electricals and at P96 vs the broad market; trailing P/E is 146.8x (P98) against a 28–45x sector range, and the price is at 86% of its 52-week range, so valuation is clearly expensive. The biggest risk is that the stock is priced for a margin recovery that the last two quarters have not shown, and no order-book or order-inflow data was available to show that the revenue growth will turn into profit.

Using EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-heavy manufacturer, the stock looks cheap at 11.3x, which is 52% below the broad-market median and at P15. Trailing P/E is 19.8x, below the 28-45x Industrials range, and the stock sits at 17% of its 52-week range. Part of that discount looks earned: new orders fell from ₹20,500 cr to ₹7,300 cr, the order book now covers 2.2x revenue versus 2.5x before, module plants ran at only 45%, and FY EPS estimates were cut 5.9% in 30 days. The feed's debt/equity of 21.4 and 16% dividend yield look like data errors, and the feed also tags the stock as IT.

fundamental.thesis: Zen Technologies makes combat-training simulators and counter-drone systems, and is a niche midcap that benefits as India shifts defence buying to domestic suppliers (about 82% of recently approved capital proposals are earmarked for Indian industry). Revenue is very uneven from quarter to quarter: Q2FY27 revenue was a record ₹345 cr, up 98.8% YoY, right after Q1FY27 fell 10.5% to ₹142 cr. That took H1FY27 revenue to ₹487 cr (+46.7%), but H1 PAT grew only 15.7% to ₹124 cr. Margins are shrinking, with H1 EBITDA margin down from 39.0% to 35.1% and PAT margin down from 32.3% to 25.5%, partly because other income fell 24%. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for order-book businesses, and the stock is expensive: EV/EBITDA is 68.3x (P94 vs peers, +193% vs the 23.3x median) and trailing P/E is 87x, well above the 28–45x Industrials range. The 32.9x forward P/E already assumes a sharp earnings recovery, and analysts raising estimates by about 4–5% only partly supports that. The biggest risk is that the ₹1,376 cr order book covers only about 1.6x trailing-12-month revenue (about ₹880 cr), and new orders arrive in lumps. That gives only around 1.5 years of visibility, so one slow quarter could hurt a stock priced for steady execution.

The latest quarter we can confidently tie to ACC is Q1 FY27, where revenue fell 8.6% YoY to ₹5,740 cr, PAT fell 60.8% to ₹147 cr and EBITDA margin was 8.5%. The Q2FY27 numbers in the trend table (₹9,197 cr revenue, ₹236 cr PAT, 113.5 MTPA capacity, ₹770/t EBITDA, down 27% YoY) appear to be Ambuja group figures, but they point the same way: flat volumes, ₹770/t is well below the healthy ₹900–1,100 band, and fuel costs are up because of the West Asia conflict. Using EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for cement, ACC trades at 9.7x with P/B of 1.15x and trailing P/E of 12.4x, all in the bottom decile of the broad market, so it is graded cheap. That cheapness is backed by falling earnings: forward P/E is above trailing, and FY EPS estimates were cut 8–10% over 90 days. The stock sits near its 52-week low, so the low multiple may be a value trap rather than a mispricing.

The yfinance Q1FY27 row (revenue ₹104.9 cr against PAT ₹73.4 cr, a 70% margin) also looks wrong on revenue. Cash conversion was weak at 0.32× operating cash flow to PAT in HY FY26. I used EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, as the sector card asks for chemicals. At 24.4× EV/EBITDA and 38.8× trailing P/E the stock looks expensive against Materials norms (12–22× P/E). However, analysts have cut this year's EPS estimates by 4.9% in 30 days and 5.6% in 90 days, while 12 of 14 still rate it a buy. That gap often comes before a de-rating. The biggest risk is that Chinese price competition keeps squeezing margins and growth in its specialty intermediates while the stock still trades at a premium multiple.

fundamental.thesis: Gravita India recycles lead, copper, aluminium and plastics, with lead still 62% of H1 revenue and the main profit driver at a 10.6% margin, while the copper segment added through the RMIL acquisition is 27% of revenue at only a 3.0% margin. Q2FY27 revenue rose 38.0% to Rs 1,427 cr, but this growth is flattered by the March 2026 RMIL deal (the organic split is not disclosed in the data provided); PAT growth slowed from +14.3% in Q1 to +6.0% at Rs 102 cr, EBITDA margin fell from 16.5% in H1FY26 to 10.0%, and CFO/PAT was -0.33x in H1FY27 with FCF of Rs -210 cr. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for a capital-intensive metals business, 24.0x looks expensive against the sector card's 5-8x for cyclical materials and the 33.2x trailing P/E is above the 12-22x Materials range, though recycling is not a direct match for those norms and the P52 peer rank is only a broad-market fallback; the 21.7x forward P/E needs strong earnings growth while FY estimates are being cut (-1.8% and next-FY -3.0% over 90 days) despite 10 of 10 buy ratings, and several feed values look unreliable, so I ignored the 64% dividend yield and the yfinance revenue of Rs 1,167 cr, read Debt/Equity of 29.93 as a probable 0.30x, and estimate the Rs 1,920 mean target at about +11-13% (price about Rs 1,700-1,725 from market cap and 52-week position) rather than +35.5%. The biggest risk is that acquired low-margin copper revenue keeps diluting margins while working capital absorbs cash, leaving little room at this valuation for further estimate cuts.

fundamental.thesis: Hindustan Zinc is India's dominant integrated zinc-lead-silver miner (Vedanta Group subsidiary) with near-monopoly status in domestic mined zinc and structural cost advantages that produce world-class EBITDA margins of 62.4% — a level no domestic peer can match. H1FY27 revenue surged 76.7% YoY to ₹28,840 cr (accelerating sharply from -4.4% in Q1FY26), PAT grew 143.4% YoY to ₹11,881 cr, and PAT margin expanded to 41.2% from 29.9% — a five-period trajectory of simultaneously accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins driven primarily by elevated zinc and silver commodity prices, with cash quality strong (CFO/PAT 1.12×). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive commodity miner, the stock trades at 10.59× — P13 among 473 peers and a 54.6% discount to the broad-market EV/EBITDA median — with trailing P/E of 17.46× squarely inside the Materials sector range (12–22×), grading cheap on peer-relative metrics, though 10.59× sits above the 5–8× typical mid-cycle range for base-metals cyclicals, signalling that some commodity-cycle-peak risk remains unpriced. The thesis is materially constrained by an unresolved ED/FEMA investigation (search and seizure June 2026, no regulatory communication as of the October 2026 filing) and SEBI observations on related party transaction disclosures — governance headwinds typical of Vedanta Group that can trigger a de-rating independent of commodity fundamentals, and are weighted heavily under the midcap governance overlay.

Jain Resource Recycling is a non-ferrous metal recycler that makes copper, lead and aluminium from scrap. It is a commodity-spread business, recently listed, and copper is now about two-thirds of its revenue. Revenue is growing fast, but much of that comes from copper prices and profit is not keeping up. H1 FY27 revenue rose 65.5% YoY to ₹6,061 cr while PAT rose only 3.1% to ₹160 cr. Taking Q1 out of H1 suggests Q2 FY27 revenue of about ₹3,337 cr (around +58% YoY, slower than Q1's +75.9%) and PAT of about ₹91 cr, which is roughly 8% lower than a year ago. EBITDA margin has fallen from 7.0% (9M FY26) to 5.7% (Q1) to 4.5% (H1), and PAT margin from 4.4% to about 2.7%. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA because the sector card says to judge cyclical, commodity-spread businesses that way. On that measure the stock looks expensive. EV/EBITDA is 25.1×, against roughly 5–8× for cyclicals at mid-cycle, and trailing P/E is 35.8×, against a 12–22× Materials benchmark. The 19.9× forward P/E depends on earnings growth, but analysts have cut those estimates by about 19% over the last 90 days. The biggest risk is that margins keep shrinking while net debt is high (about 3.3× EBITDA, debt/equity about 82%). If copper prices or recycling spreads reverse, earnings could fall sharply.

fundamental.thesis: Chambal Fertilizers is one of India's largest private urea makers. It also sells traded and complex fertilisers and crop-protection products, and it has just started a new Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN) plant at Gadepan from August 20, 2026. Its earnings depend heavily on the government subsidy rules (New Urea Policy 2015 and NBS). Growth is going the wrong way: Q1FY27 revenue was ₹5,027 cr, down 11.8% YoY, and PAT was ₹524 cr, down 4.6%, after FY26 grew 25% on traded complex fertilisers. Q2FY27 PAT margin slipped to about 9.0% from 10.4% in Q1, but the Q2 revenue figure was not extracted from the filing and the yfinance quarterly rows (Q2 revenue ₹4,367 cr) do not match the PDF figures, so the latest-quarter picture is only partly confirmed. I graded this as a capital-intensive commodity business on EV/EBITDA, which at 7.3x sits at the low end of the 5–8x mid-cycle range for cyclicals. Trailing P/E of 9.9x is below the 12–22x Materials benchmark, ROE is 20.5%, net debt is slightly negative (the 10.27 'debt/equity' looks like a percentage, given 48x interest coverage), and the stock is in the bottom decile of the broad market on every multiple, so the verdict is cheap. Cash conversion is the biggest worry: FY26 operating cash flow covered only 0.07x of PAT and receivables jumped from ₹368 cr to ₹2,075 cr, which looks like delayed subsidy payments and makes the reported earnings less solid than they appear.

fundamental.thesis: Jubilant Ingrevia is a mid-cap Indian chemicals maker with three segments: Specialty Chemicals, Nutrition (vitamin B3 and feed premixes) and Chemical Intermediates (acetyls). It is now adding CDMO capacity and has bought a 40% stake in ZettaOne, an electronics-materials business. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹1,394 cr, up 24% YoY and an all-time high, compared with low-single-digit growth through FY26 (+1.3% in Q1FY26, +5.0% for FY26). PAT rose 61% to ₹111 cr, and both PAT margin (8.0% vs 6.1–7.2% across FY26) and EBITDA margin (16.0% vs 13.6–14.8%) widened, but Q1FY27 is missing from the filings data, so the speed-up rests mainly on one quarter. I graded valuation mainly on EV/EBITDA, as the sector card says to for chemicals: at 18.1x it is far above the card's 5–8x mid-cycle range for commodity chemicals, though that range doesn't fully fit a specialty/CDMO mix; it is 22% below the broad-market median (P35), with trailing P/E of 34.6x at P48 and forward P/E of 22.3x, so I call it fair overall, not cheap. The main risks are muddy cash flow and earnings quality: finance costs jumped 85% YoY on acquisition-related borrowing, H1 FY26 earnings were weakly backed by cash (0.67x CFO/PAT, negative free cash flow), and analysts have trimmed next-year EPS estimates (−2.4% over 30 days, −3.7% over 90 days) even as they raised this year's.

fundamental.thesis: Linde India is a subsidiary of the global Linde group that makes industrial gases and also runs a lower-margin project engineering arm. Gases bring in about 71% of segment revenue at a 26.4% segment margin, while project engineering earns only 9.8%. The latest extracted quarter, Q1FY27, shows revenue of ₹694 cr, up 21.6% YoY, but PAT fell 2.4% YoY to ₹105 cr. PAT margin has slipped to 15.1% from the low-to-mid 20s in earlier periods, and the H1 EBITDA margin dropped 850 bps to 31.8%. In short, sales are growing faster but that growth is not reaching profit, and heavy capex (about 96% of H1 revenue) pushed free cash flow to -₹647 cr. Industrial gases is a utility-like business, not a steel or cement cyclical, so I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA and peer multiples. EV/EBITDA was not available, so I fell back on peer multiples: trailing P/E of 99.6x, forward P/E of 73.8x and P/B of 12.7x put it at P93/P98/P89 against the broad market, roughly 180-220% above the median, which is clearly expensive. Sell-side next-year EPS estimates have been cut about 14% over the last 30-90 days. The Q2FY27 results (filed 3 Nov) have not been extracted yet, so this view rests on Q1 and H1 data.

fundamental.thesis: Concord Biotech is a midcap maker of fermentation-based pharma ingredients and formulations, with low debt (debt/equity 0.12), though this pack does not contain enough data to judge its market position. Revenue growth has swung from -20.3% in Q2 FY26 to +26.2% in Q1 FY27 and about +25% in Q2 FY27 (derived as H1 Rs 567 cr less Q1 Rs 257 cr, or about Rs 310 cr), but this is an easy-base recovery: Q2 revenue is only back to roughly its Q2 FY25 level, implied Q2 PAT of about Rs 68 cr is up only about 7% YoY, and implied EBITDA margin has fallen to about 29% from 36.7%, while H1 cash conversion stayed healthy at 1.32x CFO/PAT. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, cross-checked with P/E because no tight listed peers were available, the stock looks expensive at 37.0x EV/EBITDA (P78 and 59% above the broad-market median) and 50.8x trailing P/E against a 28-40x pharma range; the 34.4x forward P/E already prices in a strong profit recovery, and the +23.8% sell-side upside looks unreliable because the Rs 1,520 mean target is only about 5% above the roughly Rs 1,450 price implied by market cap and EPS. The biggest risk is that profit does not catch up with revenue, since FY27 EPS estimates were cut 2.8% in the last 30 days and the valuation leaves little room for further margin slippage; confidence is also limited because the FY26 revenue and PAT rows appear overstated tenfold, the 51% dividend yield is clearly wrong, and no sector KPIs or management guidance were available.

Anthem Biosciences is a contract research, development and manufacturing (CRDMO) company with a smaller specialty-ingredients arm; CRDMO made up 84% of H1 FY27 revenue. It has a clean record with regulators (USFDA, TGA, ANVISA), net cash of ₹1,538 cr, and FY26 cash flow of 1.48x PAT. Revenue has gone from +15.0% growth in FY26 to a -7.2% fall in H1 FY27 (₹1,012 cr). Q1 fell 22.6% to ₹418 cr. Q2 recovered to about ₹594 cr, roughly +8% YoY, a figure we worked out from the H1 and Q1 numbers. H1 PAT rose 7.2% to ₹331 cr, a 30.2% margin, but part of that margin comes from other income booked inside EBITDA (₹84 cr, about 17% of EBITDA). We graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the measure the sector card favours for capital-heavy CDMO businesses. At 50.8x EV/EBITDA and 76x trailing P/E, the stock is far above the 28–40x pharma P/E range and sits around P86–P93 against peers on every multiple, so it is expensive even allowing a China+1 CDMO premium. The analyst mean target is only 0.7% above the current price, and next-year earnings estimates have been cut 3.6% over 90 days.

fundamental.thesis: Jubilant Pharmova is a diversified Indian pharma company spanning CDMO Sterile Injectables, Allergy Immunotherapy, Radiopharma, and Generics — a complex, multi-segment business with meaningful US and Canada exposure. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue accelerated to +17.3% YoY (₹2,229 cr), continuing a multi-quarter re-acceleration from +9.8% in Q1FY26, but PAT collapsed 45% YoY to ₹56 cr as EBITDA margins contracted sharply from 15.9% (Q1FY26) to 12.0%, with CDMO Sterile Injectables margins imploding from 11% to 1.4% and the Generics segment swinging to a ₹10 cr operating loss — a dangerous divergence between topline and bottom-line trajectories. Trailing P/E of 38.8× sits near the top of the pharma sector benchmark range (28–40×) on deeply-depressed earnings; EV/EBITDA of 14.17× (P23 percentile vs broad peers) looks more attractive but still reflects deteriorating EBITDA; forward P/E of 19.16× embeds a steep earnings recovery that consensus has already cut by ~25% in the last 30 days, making the 'cheap-on-forward' narrative fragile. The biggest risk is a dual FDA compliance overhang — OAI at Montreal (remediation expenses of ₹535 mn already booked, manufacturing suspended) plus a live USFDA Spokane update — alongside a GST show-cause notice and a high debt/equity ratio (50.94×), any one of which could derail the assumed margin recovery.

Lloyds Metals and Energy is a fast-growing midcap that mines iron ore and makes pellets and sponge iron (DRI). It is in the middle of a heavy capacity build-out, so its earnings swing with iron-ore and steel spreads. Subtracting Q1FY27 from H1FY27 (₹13,009 cr revenue, ₹2,791 cr PAT) gives Q2FY27 revenue of about ₹5,655 cr (+52.5% YoY vs ₹3,707 cr) and PAT of about ₹1,057 cr (+86% YoY vs ₹567 cr). But revenue growth has slowed sharply, from +204.5% in Q3FY26 and +208.6% in Q1FY27 to +52.5%. Revenue fell about 23% and PAT about 39% from Q1, partly due to the monsoon season, and PAT margin dropped from 23.6% to about 18.7%. Using EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive cyclical, the stock trades at 19.1×, far above the 5–8× mid-cycle norm for steel and mining names. Trailing P/E of 26.3× is also above the 12–22× Materials range, so I grade it expensive. The 12.1× forward P/E and analysts' +38% upgrades to FY earnings estimates only hold up if the new capacity delivers on time, and the stock is already at 84% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is the balance sheet: debt/equity of about 1.45×, FY26 free cash flow of -₹1,853 cr and fresh NCD (bond) raises mean any delay in commissioning or a fall in iron-ore prices would hurt both earnings and the leverage story.

fundamental.thesis: Max Healthcare is one of India's largest listed hospital chains, with about 6,100 network beds running at more than 75% occupancy. Taking H1 FY27 minus Q1, Q2 FY27 revenue comes to about ₹2,569 cr, up about 20% YoY, and EBITDA margin has widened from 26.8% to 28.2% over the trend window. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-intensive, lease-heavy business, 7.41x (P6 vs a broad-market peer set, not cinema peers) with P/B of 1.27x and a price at 14% of the 52-week range grades cheap, with modest confidence because the 53.06x trailing P/E appears to exclude H1 FY27 profit, the 16.16x forward P/E needs earnings to roughly triple, ROE is only 2.4%, and the consensus '+7.7% upside' implies a price near Rs 1,524, well above the Rs 1,250 52-week high. The biggest risks are that a weak film slate hits a high fixed-cost business and that the recovery proves less durable than the +27.6% estimate upgrades suggest; separately, the promoter's Regulation 31 disclosure dated 2026-11-03 needs checking for any share pledge, and no footfall, ticket-price or management guidance data was available.

TBO Tek runs a B2B travel-distribution platform that connects travel agents worldwide to hotel and airline inventory, and since the Classic Vacations acquisition it also has a North American leisure arm. In Q2FY27 reported revenue of ₹866 cr grew 52.5% YoY, slower than Q1's +81%, and most of that headline growth comes from the acquisition: organic GTV grew 22% and organic gross profit 21%, while organic adjusted EBITDA grew 36%. Consolidated EBITDA margin has contracted from 22.5% to 17.6% over the trend window, and the last PAT margin we have is 9.0% in Q1FY27, down from about 14% a year earlier, because the lower-margin Classic Vacations business now makes up more of the mix. Q2 PAT was not available from the filings, and the revenue scale in the trend table does not match the yfinance rows, so treat the absolute figures with some caution. On valuation, the sector card says platform names should be judged on EV/EBITDA and growth delivery, not P/E alone: at 39.3x EV/EBITDA (P81 vs the broad market) and 68.4x trailing P/E (P83), with the stock at 88.8% of its 52-week range, the shares look expensive even though the forward P/E of 33.5x assumes strong earnings growth. The biggest risk is that the price assumes perfection while FY EPS estimates were cut about 10% in the last 30 days and governance issues are piling up: an unprovisioned ED/FEMA penalty of about ₹22 cr, an ₹8.1 cr employee fraud at an overseas subsidiary, and ₹8.9 cr of FX losses.

fundamental.thesis: Endurance Technologies makes auto parts, mainly for two-wheelers in India, including suspension, braking, transmission and aluminium castings. Taking H1 minus Q1 gives an implied Q2 revenue of about ₹4,811 cr (+33.5% YoY, up from +29.6% in Q1) and PAT of about ₹274 cr (+21% YoY, up from +8% in Q1). Profits are growing much more slowly than sales, though. EBITDA margin fell from 13.1% in Q1 to about 12.1% in Q2, PAT margin is stuck near 5.6–5.7%, and analysts cut their FY earnings estimates by 4% over the last 90 days. fundamental.thesis: ABFRL is a midcap fashion retailer that owns Pantaloons (value retail, 399 stores), an ethnic-wear portfolio including TCNS and Jaypore, the TMRW digital brands and a small luxury arm, with about 1,286 stores in total. Losses got worse: Q2 PAT was about ₹-376 cr, a margin of about -18.5%, against -12.3% in Q1. H1 EBITDA fell 28% YoY to ₹130 cr, and free cash flow was ₹-288 cr. The business is loss-making, so P/E means nothing here; I graded on EV/EBITDA and P/B. EV/EBITDA is 18.2x, against 23.3x for the broad-market median (P36). P/B is 1.28x (P7), which looks cheap, but return on equity is -12.7%, so we call valuation fair, not cheap, even though the stock sits near its 52-week low (19% of range). The biggest risk is that the turnaround keeps failing: no segment makes money at the profit line, the ethnic segment's margin is -23%, and net debt of ₹1,334 cr is about 10x EBITDA.

The biggest risk is that margins stay squeezed by copper and commodity costs, rising crude and a new-plant ramp-up, so revenue keeps growing without profit following it.

fundamental.thesis: Ola Electric is India's largest EV two-wheeler OEM with vertically integrated battery ambitions (Ola Cell Technologies), but it remains deeply pre-profit and is facing a severe revenue downturn — Q1FY27 revenue fell 45% YoY to ₹455cr (from ₹828cr in Q1FY26), with PAT margin contracting sharply from -51.7% in Q1FY26 to -73.8% in Q1FY27, suggesting unit economics are deteriorating, not improving, as scale has shrunk. The single biggest risk is the auditor-qualified going concern assessment: management itself flagged negative operating cash flow of ₹215cr in Q1FY27, and a fresh rights issue announced September 28, 2026 confirms that the company requires continuous external capital — dilution and solvency risk are both live.

fundamental.thesis: Schaeffler India is a precision components manufacturer (bearings, transmission systems, clutch parts) for automotive and industrial customers, leveraging its German parent's technology IP and commanding ~79% of revenue from the Mobility segment with a quality premium over domestic-only ancillaries. H1 2026 showed revenue growth of +18.1% YoY to ₹5,346 cr and PAT growth of +19.1% to ₹642 cr, with EBITDA margin expanding from 19.6% to 20.1% across the tracked periods — an accelerating trajectory, though CFO/PAT of 0.61× is borderline weak and the ₹547 cr dividend paid against only ₹389 cr CFO raises a capital-allocation flag. The biggest risk is the premium valuation built on an uninterrupted growth story, which offers no margin of safety if growth decelerates due to auto-sector cyclicality, rising crude input costs, ongoing subsidiary losses (KRSV PAT −₹32 cr H1), or EV disruption of traditional drivetrain demand.

JSW Dulux (formerly Akzo Nobel India, bought by the JSW Group in Dec 2025) is a mid-sized decorative and industrial paints maker. It has been gaining volume, but its profit margins are under heavy pressure. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹1,927 cr, up 5.8% YoY as reported and up 20% on a like-for-like basis that excludes the divested Powder Coatings and IRC divisions, with volume up 23%. Reported revenue growth has improved from -4.0% (Q1FY26) to -2.8% (Q1FY27) to +5.8% (H1FY27). Over the same window PAT margin has fallen from 9.2% to 8.3% to 7.8%, and gross margin fell 1,180bp YoY to 35.4% as raw-material inflation outran price increases. Implied Q2 PAT of about ₹71 cr is below Q1's ₹80 cr. I used forward P/E rather than trailing P/E. The 7.45× trailing P/E and the P4 'cheap vs peers' rank are not real: they are inflated by the ₹1,874 cr one-off gain from the divestiture in H1 FY26, and the reported -91.5% H1 PAT drop is distorted by that same gain. On forward P/E of 31.3× (P67 vs the broad market) and P/B of 6.0×, the stock is fair: below listed paint leaders but not cheap for a business whose margins are falling. Sell-side FY-EPS estimates have been cut 8.8% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that crude is near $91 and rising, which pushes up paint raw-material costs and could cut margins further while the new JSW owners push for market share.

fundamental.thesis: Allied Blenders and Distillers is a midcap Indian spirits maker, with a Rs 17,700 cr market value and thin margins on reported revenue that includes excise duty. Revenue growth has improved from -6.2% in FY26 to +1.9% in Q1 FY27 and +4.3% to Rs 3,903 cr in H1 FY27 (about +7% to Rs 2,094 cr in Q2, derived from the H1 and Q1 figures), but H1 PAT fell 3.6% to Rs 114 cr, the 2.9% PAT margin is slightly below H1 FY26's 3.2%, and the data shows neither volume growth nor a reliable gross margin trend. Using the sector card's FMCG P/E norm, cross-checked with broad-market EV/EBITDA and P/B ranks because there are no tight peers, the stock is expensive at 77.3x trailing P/E against 40-65x, with EV/EBITDA of 34.5x and P/B of 10.7x against 13.6% ROE; the 39.9x forward P/E implies EPS nearly doubling while near-term estimates are slipping about 1%. The biggest risk is a valuation de-rating if profit does not catch up with those expectations, and conviction is limited by data conflicts: implied Q2 PAT of Rs 65 cr vs Rs 71.5 cr on yfinance, a likely misstated 86% dividend yield, debt/equity of 68.25 that probably means 0.68x rather than 68x, and a price implied by the consensus upside (about Rs 694) that does not match the one implied by the 52-week position (about Rs 633).

fundamental.thesis: Radico Khaitan is a premium-led Indian spirits maker whose Magic Moments brand holds about 60% of the Indian vodka market. Q2FY27 net revenue rose 16.8% YoY to Rs 1,745 cr and PAT rose 66.1% to Rs 231 cr; the table's 'decelerating' and 'contracting' signals are unreliable because it mixes revenue before and after excise duty, but on a net basis revenue growth did slow from +24.7% in FY26 while EBITDA margin improved from 16.8% to 20.4%, with Prestige & Above volumes up 35.8%, Regular & Others down 9.7%, and total volume growth (+7.2%) trailing price/mix (+9.6%). Using P/E as the main yardstick with EV/EBITDA as a cross-check, the valuation is expensive: the 81.8x trailing P/E appears to use FY26 PAT and falls to about 62x on my estimate of trailing-12-month PAT (about Rs 796 cr), near the top of the sector card's 40-65x range, while forward P/E is 51.1x, EV/EBITDA is 40.3x, broad-market ranks are P82-P93 and the stock sits at 96% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is that this price needs the premium growth and roughly 20% margin guidance to hold while grain costs, state policy and higher inventory (H1 CFO/PAT 0.82x) create pressure; three snapshot fields also look unreliable, as the 15% dividend yield and 20.94 debt/equity look like unit errors and the +16.1% consensus upside does not match the roughly Rs 3,690 price implied by market cap, and the October 28 earnings call transcript is not reflected here.

BLS International runs outsourced visa and consular processing for foreign governments, where it earns high margins (H1FY27 segment margin 39.7%). It also has a fast-growing but low-margin Digital Services and e-governance arm (H1FY27 revenue ₹793 cr, up 50% YoY, at only a 6.2% margin). Revenue growth picked up from +25.3% YoY in Q1FY27 to +32.0% in Q2FY27 (₹973 cr), but profit is not keeping pace. Q2 PAT rose only 8.6% to ₹202 cr, PAT margin fell from 25.2% to 20.8% YoY, and EBITDA margin dropped from about 30% in FY26 to 25.5%. The causes are the shift toward the low-margin digital business and costs from the Atyati and Trefeddian Hotel acquisitions. On valuation we used EV/EBITDA and P/E rather than the sector card's 60-100x consumer-discretionary multiples, because this is a services contractor, not a premium consumer franchise. At 10.2x EV/EBITDA and 13.8x trailing P/E (11.0x forward), the stock sits around the cheapest 11% of the broad market and well below the market median of 35x P/E, and net cash of ₹1,665 cr (about 17% of market cap) supports that. So we grade it cheap, though the stock near its 52-week low shows the market is already pricing in the falling margins. The main risk is that margins keep sliding as the digital business grows and acquired businesses are integrated, which would leave earnings flat even while revenue grows.

fundamental.thesis: Tata Consumer Products is India's second-largest branded foods-and-beverages company, with leading positions in tea (Tata Tea, Tetley) and salt (Tata Salt), supplemented by an inorganic expansion into nutrition and adjacent FMCG via Capital Foods, Soulfull, and Organic India acquisitions. Q1FY27 revenue grew +11.9% YoY to ₹5,349 cr — a meaningful deceleration from +15.0% in Q3FY26 — though PAT surged +28.8% YoY to ₹427 cr (margin 8.0% vs 7.0% a year ago), powered by lower tea input costs and gross-margin expansion from 40.1% to 42.7%; volume growth in the India business was ~13%, solid but to be weighed against the sector card's caution on >10% volume claims. At a trailing P/E of 60.51× — at the upper bound of the FMCG benchmark range of 40–60× and ranked P78 among broad-market peers — the stock screens as expensive even near its 52-week low; however, a forward P/E of 41.78× (31% below trailing) signals the market is pricing in a meaningful earnings step-up from acquisition integration and tea-cost tailwinds. The principal risk is sustained revenue growth deceleration toward sub-10% alongside a reported Debt/Equity of 12.16 (reflecting heavy acquisition financing), which leaves the stock highly exposed to multiple compression if earnings delivery disappoints or high-rate conditions pressure interest coverage.

UNO Minda is a domestic auto-component supplier that sells lighting, switches, alloy wheels, sunroofs and EV parts to Indian two-wheeler and car makers, so it benefits from premiumisation and the rising share of EVs. Growth is accelerating: H1 FY27 revenue was ₹12,212 cr (+31.3% YoY) and PAT was ₹756 cr (+19.7%), up from Q1 FY27's +23.8% revenue and +2.1% PAT. Subtracting Q1 from H1 gives a Q2 of about ₹6,655 cr revenue and ₹440 cr PAT, in line with the company's own press release reporting 38% YoY growth in both. Profitability is not keeping pace, though: EBITDA margin fell from 11.76% to 10.69% YoY and H1 free cash flow was negative (₹-96 cr) after ₹806 cr of capex. Using P/E and EV/EBITDA for an auto ancillary, the stock looks expensive: trailing P/E of 53× and forward P/E of 35.5× are both well above the 18–28× auto range, EV/EBITDA is 29×, P/B is 10×, and it sits at P71–P82 versus the broad market. The stock is near the low end of its 52-week range (27%) and the average analyst target is about 1% below the current price. The main risk is that the high multiple is priced for growth while margins and cash conversion keep slipping.

fundamental.thesis: Affle 3i is a mobile ad-tech platform that sells cost-per-converted-user (CPCU) advertising, mainly in India and emerging markets; it is a platform business, not a headcount-based IT services firm. Growth is steady but not speeding up. H1 FY27 revenue rose 20.8% YoY to ₹1,531 cr and PAT rose 19.5% to ₹258 cr. Subtracting Q1 from H1 gives Q2 FY27 revenue of about ₹784 cr (around +21% YoY) and PAT of about ₹130 cr (about 16.6% margin), so YoY growth has held in a tight 19–21% band for six periods with PAT margin flat at 16.6–17.2%. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA (31.6x) plus forward P/E (29.7x), not the static IT-services P/E table, because Affle is a platform business. Trailing P/E of 46x is above the 22–30x IT range and about 31% above the broad-market median (P66). Forward P/E is at the top of that range, and the stock sits at 25.5% of its 52-week range. For a business growing about 20% with a ₹1,752 cr net cash cushion, I grade it fair, not cheap. Several things just added risk. The company agreed to acquire Israel-listed Perion Network, cancelled its earnings call citing a 'material development', and still has a ₹1,358 cr Bobble investment caught in insolvency, with a Supreme Court hearing on 25 Nov 2026. Cash conversion has also weakened to 0.65x CFO/PAT in H1.

fundamental.thesis: JSW Energy is a large private power producer with 15.1 GW of installed capacity, about 61% of it renewable, and a stated path to 30 GW by 2030 built on long-term power contracts. In Q2FY27, revenue rose 24.2% YoY to Rs 6,658 cr and PAT rose 38.5% to Rs 1,141 cr (17.1% margin, EBITDA margin 58.7%), but revenue growth has slowed from +78.6% in Q1FY26 and +59.8% in Q2FY26 as acquisitions enter the base, and Q1FY27 is missing from the trend table while the signals mix annual and quarterly rows. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-intensive business, valuation grades expensive at 17.0x, backed by a trailing P/E of 45.1x against the 10-18x Utilities benchmark and a P/B of 3.29x against ROE of only 8.8%; the 'fair' broad-market peer read carries little weight because it has no tight industry peers. The biggest risk is that net leverage of 4.94x operational and 5.55x total, above the 4.5x target, must fund Rs 20,000 cr of FY27 capex while finance costs are up 14% and FY EPS estimates have been cut 3.1% over 90 days.

Latent View Analytics is a mid-cap data-analytics and AI consulting firm with about 1,800 employees and 40 Fortune 500 clients; it is still growing much faster than tier-1 Indian IT, which is close to flat. Growth is slowing quarter by quarter, though. Revenue growth fell from +27.3% YoY in H1FY26 and +24.3% in FY26 to +14.2% in Q2FY27 (₹294 cr). Q2 PAT was ₹48 cr (+6.1% YoY), and H1FY27 PAT was flat at -0.8% even though revenue grew 17.7%. Margins are shrinking because employee costs rose 21.8% YoY and now take 68.8% of revenue, and outside Industrials (+21.4%) the segments are barely growing (Financial Services +3.5%, CPG/Retail +2.7%). On valuation I used the IT sector P/E range plus EV/EBITDA. Trailing P/E is 32.3x, a little above the 22–30x IT range. Forward P/E is 22.1x and EV/EBITDA is 24.2x, close to the broad-market median (about P50). That makes it fair overall, not cheap, since estimates are being cut. The biggest worry is earnings quality: in H1 only about 26% of profit turned into operating cash (CFO/PAT 0.26x, down from 0.60x), and analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 6% over 90 days. Both suggest the growth premium could shrink further.

fundamental.thesis: Physicswallah is a fast-growing Indian test-prep company that sells low-priced online courses and is expanding offline coaching centres, and it is still only around breakeven. The latest numbers we have are for Q1 FY27: revenue of ₹1,054 cr, up 24.4% YoY, against 35.0% growth for full-year FY26 (₹3,900 cr), so growth looks to be slowing. EBITDA margin was only 4.9% in Q1 FY27 versus 14.1% for FY26, and FY26 ended with a net loss of ₹24 cr (-0.6% PAT margin), though part of that margin gap is likely seasonal since Q1 is usually weak for coaching businesses. The Q2 FY27 results filed on 2026-11-04 have not been extracted yet, so this view is stale by one quarter. Because the business is barely profitable, I graded valuation on EV/sales and EV/EBITDA rather than P/E: price-to-sales of 8.43x and EV/EBITDA of 72.1x (P96 vs the broad market, about 3x the 23.3x median) are expensive for a business with slowing growth, unproven offline unit economics and -0.8% ROE. The biggest risk is that growth keeps slowing while the offline build-out and the Utkarsh Classes acquisition squeeze margins, which would knock the rich multiple down sharply.
